      # ROAS deploy scripts

      Agent-facing entry points for ROAS production deploys. Secrets live in gitignored `scripts/roas/roas-secrets.env` (template: `roas-secrets.env.template`).

      ## Personal → org Meetings / spaces clone (one-time)

      `clone-personal-spaces-to-org.py` clones Dylan's personal Meetings (items + Fathom Meeting Log) into ROAS org General, moves CEO HQ + Sales Pipeline into org General, disables the personal Fathom automation, and sets Fathom auto-ingest billing to the ROAS org.

      ```bash
      python3 scripts/roas/clone-personal-spaces-to-org.py --dry-run
      python3 scripts/roas/clone-personal-spaces-to-org.py
      ```

      Idempotent: skips clone if org Meetings already exists; skips moves already on org General.

      ## ROAS Company Wiki rebuild

      `rebuild-company-wiki.py` upgrades the existing ROAS Internal wiki records in place. It uses
      locally maintained, human-authored operating blueprints; private ROAS source content is not sent
      to an external model. Dry-run and audit modes are read-only, and the script refuses any database
      host other than the configured ROAS production project.

      ```bash
      # Validate every process without writing
      python3 scripts/roas/rebuild-company-wiki.py

      # Update one category, then rebuild the six navigation pages
      python3 scripts/roas/rebuild-company-wiki.py --category="PAID MEDIA & ADVERTISING" --apply
      python3 scripts/roas/rebuild-company-wiki.py --navigation --apply

      # Verify the complete 84-process / 6-navigation topology and content contract
      python3 scripts/roas/rebuild-company-wiki.py --audit
      ```

      The process updates existing records only. Every SOP must pass the required-section, ordered
      procedure, evidence, decision-table, QA, troubleshooting, escalation, and minimum-depth checks
      before any write occurs. It does not approve or modify Company Cortex signals.

      ## Fly agent runtime (`roas-runtimes`)

      **Always use the script — do not run raw `flyctl deploy`.**

      ```bash
      bash scripts/roas/deploy-fly-runtimes.sh
      ```

      What it does:

      1. Applies section-9 secrets via `apply-fly-secrets.sh`
      2. **Swaps root `.dockerignore` → `docker/fly.dockerignore` for the build, then restores** (see below)
      3. Deploys from repo root with `docker/fly.roas.runtime.toml` + `docker/Dockerfile`
      4. Prints `/api/health/deep` and fails when OpenClaw or auth is unreachable

      Post-deploy smoke:

      ```bash
      SMOKE_FLY=1 bash scripts/roas/smoke-deploy.sh
      ```

      ### Why the `.dockerignore` swap?

      Root `.dockerignore` excludes `apps/openclaw` and `apps/agent-api` so Railway `mission-worker` snapshots stay small. The Fly runtime image **needs** those apps.

      Fly/Depot uses BuildKit, which reads `.dockerignore` from the build context root only. **`flyctl deploy --ignorefile` is ignored** ([flyctl#3870](https://github.com/superfly/flyctl/issues/3870)). Raw `flyctl deploy` fails with:

      ```text
      "/apps/openclaw": not found
      "/apps/agent-api": not found
      ```

      `deploy-fly-runtimes.sh` handles the swap automatically. Do not deploy Fly runtimes with bare `flyctl deploy`.

      ### Config files

      | File                            | Purpose                                                                |
      | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
      | `docker/fly.roas.runtime.toml`  | Fly app config (ROAS only; `docker/fly.runtime.toml` is Vibey staging) |
      | `docker/fly.dockerignore`       | Build context for Fly — includes openclaw + agent-api                  |
      | `docker/openclaw.json`          | Baked into image; invalid plugins break `/v1/responses`                |
      | `scripts/roas/roas-secrets.env` | Section 9 → Fly secrets                                                |

      ### Runtime requirements

      - `AGENT_RUNTIME_MODE=shared` (section 9)
      - `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18789` (in-container gateway, not public URL)
      - `OPENROUTER_INTERACTIVE_API_KEY` for interactive Chat requests
      - `OPENROUTER_BACKGROUND_API_KEY` for Mission and Brain requests
      - `OPENROUTER_MEDIA_API_KEY` for media and image requests
      - `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` remains the temporary fallback while the scoped keys are rolled out
      - **One machine** for shared mode (agent registration is per-machine)

      The scoped OpenRouter credentials are injected only for the active request and are
      never persisted in OpenClaw sessions. Section 9 supplies all three scopes to the Fly
      runtime. The API deployment also needs the background and media scopes for direct
      analysis, billing reconciliation, and image calls. Rotate any credential pasted into
      chat before adding it to `roas-secrets.env` or a production provider.

      The image build runs OpenClaw's plugin-aware config validation after all runtime
      plugins are installed. An unknown plugin now fails the build before Fly can
      release it.

      Fly checks `/api/health/deep`, which returns a non-2xx response when OpenClaw or
      auth is unreachable. `/api/health` remains the lightweight process-health route
      for diagnostics during startup.

      ## Other scripts

      | Script                                 | Use                                                               |
      | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
      | `apply-fly-secrets.sh`                 | Re-import section 9 only                                          |
      | `smoke-deploy.sh`                      | Post-Vercel + optional Fly checks (also runs env-freshness)       |
      | `deploy-railway-workers.sh`            | mission-worker / queue-worker (manual steps)                      |
      | `apply-migrations-resilient.sh`        | ROAS Supabase migrations                                          |
      | `verify-roas-runtime-profiles.sql`     | Drift audit — fails if any profile/pool still routes to Vibey     |
      | `verify-vercel-env-freshness.sh`       | Guard — confirms critical env vars predate current prod build     |
      | `audit-page-grader-campaign-spaces.py` | Read-only Page Grader mapping, Space, and Meta provenance audit   |
      | `audit_slack_brain_pipeline.py`        | Slack capture/import/Brain/index/retrieval audit and gated replay |

      ### Slack Campaign Brain audit and recovery

      Run the pipeline audit against one mapping before and after rollout. It reports
      raw Slack observations, the database job status versus the terminal status
      inside Atlas's response (including JSON-encoded nested envelopes), Campaign Brain memory/embedding coverage, and the
      mapping cursor. Add a probe to execute the same semantic search RPC used by
      Brain retrieval and optionally require an expected phrase in the top ten.

      ```bash
      python3 scripts/roas/audit_slack_brain_pipeline.py --mapping-id=<mapping-uuid>
      python3 scripts/roas/audit_slack_brain_pipeline.py --mapping-id=<mapping-uuid> \
        --lexical-query="approved non-sensitive phrase" --expect="expected phrase"
      python3 scripts/roas/audit_slack_brain_pipeline.py --mapping-id=<mapping-uuid> \
        --probe-query="What did the client ask us to track?" --expect="bookings" \
        --require-healthy
      ```

      The lexical probe stays inside Supabase. The semantic probe sends only its query
      text to the configured embedding provider; use it only with an approved,
      non-sensitive test query.

      Recovery is read-only unless `--apply` is supplied. Run it only after the
      fail-closed importer is deployed. It requeues at most 25 falsely successful
      periods at a time, never replays genuine skips, selects only the newest row when
      historical duplicates share a dedupe key, and skips a period if a live import
      wins the race to become active.

      ```bash
      python3 scripts/roas/audit_slack_brain_pipeline.py --org-id=<org-uuid> \
        --repair-poisoned --repair-limit=25
      python3 scripts/roas/audit_slack_brain_pipeline.py --org-id=<org-uuid> \
        --repair-poisoned --repair-limit=25 --apply --fixed-runtime-deployed
      ```

      The root `.railwayignore` keeps Railway CLI mission-worker uploads aligned with
      the mission-worker Docker build context. Do not remove the other-app exclusions:
      tracked files in those apps are not part of the worker image and may include
      machine-local symlink fixtures that the Railway uploader cannot archive.

      ### Drift guardrails (Phase 4)

      Vercel bakes env vars at **build time**, so adding a var without redeploying leaves
      production running without it (this bit us on `FLY_RUNTIME_APP` and `WORKER_SECRET`).

      ```bash
      # Confirm no profile/machine still points at Vibey/Railway/govibey (expect verdict OK):
      bash scripts/roas/apply-via-supabase-api.sh scripts/roas/verify-roas-runtime-profiles.sql

      # Confirm critical env vars were set before the current prod build:
      bash scripts/roas/verify-vercel-env-freshness.sh
      ```

      `smoke-deploy.sh` runs the env-freshness guard automatically when `roas-secrets.env`
      is present (set `SMOKE_ENV=0` to skip). Pass `AGENT_SLUG=<slug>` to also check the
      `agents.roas.io` public-agent proxy.

    status: Completed · exit 0
      7:Audit whether artifacts or Space items created by agents while running inside a task reliably appear in both places users expect:
      12:This audit covers the task-agent path, the OpenClaw tool stream bridge, backend artifact action results, frontend content-block-to-deliverable mapping, and the reported production task `d6a1b64a-ab00-4bab-87a3-06cb521b3fbb`.
      16:- The production test only created documents plus one follow-up task item. No funnels, presentations, ads, media, forms, or posts were created in that run.
      17:- 2026-06-25 update: task completion now reconciles scoped persisted outputs after the stream merge. The readback covers Space Docs, created Space items/tasks, offers, avatars, sequences, renderable presentations, renderable funnels/websites, social posts, ads/ad sets/ad campaigns, forms, flows, task-linked emails, and media assets.
      19:- The frontend can convert `artifact_preview`, `document_card`, `media_asset`, `pdf_file`, `docx_file`, `project_preview`, `widget_preview`, and `browser_screenshot` blocks into task deliverables, but not every backend output emits or persists enough scope to reconstruct one.
      21:Critical conclusion: the old document-only fallback has been replaced with a scoped generic readback for the main persisted artifact families; unsupported or unscoped producer actions still need targeted cleanup before the platform can claim every possible durable output has a DB fallback.
      25:1. Backend artifact action executes through `ArtifactActionExecutionService`.
      29:5. `TaskAgentArtifactOutputsService` adds missing scoped persisted output blocks for supported artifact tables, task-linked emails, media assets, Space Docs, and created Space items.
      39:| Offer via `create_offer` | `artifact_preview: offer` | `offer` | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
      40:| Ad via `create_ad` | `artifact_preview: ad` | `ad` or `image` if image URL exists | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
      41:| Ad campaign via `create_ad_campaign` | `artifact_preview: ad-campaign` | `ad_campaign` | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
      42:| Funnel via `create_funnel` | `artifact_preview: funnel` | `funnel` | Yes, when renderable by home page/pages/files | Covered for renderable rows |
      43:| Funnel page via `add_funnel_page` | `artifact_preview: funnel` with `funnelPageId` | `funnel` | Yes, via parent funnel renderability | Covered |
      44:| Presentation via `create_presentation` | `artifact_preview: presentation` | `presentation` | Yes, when generated HTML or files exist | Covered for renderable rows |
      45:| Sequence via `create_sequence` | `artifact_preview: sequence` | `sequence` | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
      46:| Avatar via `create_avatar` | `artifact_preview: avatar` | `avatar` or `image` if image URL exists | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
      47:| Email via `save_email` | `artifact_preview: email` | `email` | Yes, when linked to the task `source_item_id` | Covered |
      48:| Social post via `create_social_post` | `artifact_preview: social-post` | `social_post` or media if image/video URL exists | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
      49:| Blog post via `create_blog_post` | `artifact_preview: blog-post` | `blog_post` or `image` if cover exists | No | Stream-dependent |
      55:| Out-of-catalog or unscoped artifact previews | No safe task completion reconciliation when the durable row lacks task Space scope or the output has no stable previewable persisted row. | A successfully created artifact can still be absent if the stream block is missed and DB readback cannot safely identify it. | P0 |
      58:| Forms | `create_form`, `publish_form`, and `attach_form_asset` return form data/URL only; task readback now covers scoped created form rows. | Producer-side blocks are still missing, but task completion can recover created forms. | P1 |
      59:| Tasks / generic Space items | `create_task` creates `space_items` but returns raw task data only; task readback now covers non-doc Space items created in the same scoped run. | Producer-side blocks are still missing, but task completion can recover created task/custom item rows. | P1 |
      60:| Missions | `create_mission` creates/ensures Mission view and indexes the source but returns raw mission data only. No block or mapper support. | Chat-created missions can exist without a task output card. | P1 |
      62:| Flows | `create_flow_draft` and `publish_flow` return raw `space_automations`; task readback now covers scoped rows created by the task actor. | Producer-side blocks are still missing, but task completion can recover created flow rows. | P1 |
      63:| Projects/code artifacts | Frontend supports `project_preview`, but `create_project` returns the main API result and does not synthesize `project_preview`. | Code/project outputs are not guaranteed in task deliverables. | P1 |
      64:| Websites | `create_website` is implemented through the funnel path and emits `artifact_preview: funnel`; frontend has a `website` deliverable type but the block contract does not expose `website`. | Website outputs are typed as funnels in task deliverables. | P2 |
      65:| Visual docs | `generate_visual_html` emits `artifact_preview: visual-doc`; frontend block union accepts it, but deliverable mapper does not map it. | Visual docs can render in chat but not become typed task deliverables. | P2 |
      66:| Email sequence emails | `add_sequence_email` emits an `artifact_preview` with `artifactType: sequence` and the parent sequence id, not the sequence email id/type. | Individual email outputs inside a sequence are attributed to the sequence, not the email draft. | P2 |

      apps/agent-api/src/modules/brain/evals/user-work/logs/user-work-run-2026-05-27T11-01-10-021Z.json:5488:        "finalAnswer": "Here's what the brain has on Cloverkin lifecycle rules, synthesized into actionable send-window rules for Sara this week.\n\n---\n\n## Cloverkin Lifecycle Send-Window Rules\n**Owner: Sara | Effective: This week**\n\n---\n\n### The Non-Negotiable\n\n> \"I would rather lose the visit than send a marketing email a patient finds in their inbox the day after a hard appointment.\"\n> *— Dr. Marisol Vega*\n\nThis is not a preference. It is a trust violation rule. Missing the send window is better than breaking it.\n\n---\n\n### Rule 1: 48-Hour Post-Visit Blackout\n\n**No marketing send within 48 hours of any patient appointment.**\n\n- Pull the visit calendar before finalizing any send list.\n- Suppress any patient with an appointment in the prior 48 hours.\n- This applies to all send types: nurture, re-engagement, check-in.\n- The lifecycle tool has this enforced in logic already. Verify it is active before any batch goes out.\n\n---\n\n### Rule 2: No Urgency Modifiers\n\nRemove any language that creates time pressure. Cohort nurture was only approved after urgency modifiers were stripped. The same bar applies here. Words like \"last chance,\" \"act now,\" \"don't miss\" do not survive the bedside test.\n\n---\n\n### Rule 3: The Bedside Test (Copy Gate)\n\nBefore any email goes to send, read it imagining a patient at 11pm after a difficult appointment. Ask: does this lower their heart rate or raise it?\n\nIf a clinician would wince reading it aloud, it does not ship.\n\n---\n\n### Rule 4: Clinical Outcome Language = Escalate\n\nAny copy that mentions patient outcomes, results, or clinical claims triggers a double review: Maya (brand voice) plus James (clinical). Do not send until both are logged. This is not a late gate — it is the brief.\n\n---\n\n### Rule 5: Paid Has a Two-Week Organic Window\n\nCloverkin metro posts are on a two-week organic window before any paid talk. If a lifecycle message is being considered for paid amplification, it needs two weeks of organic proof first. Flag anything this week that is approaching that window.\n\n---\n\n### Rule 6: When Timing Is Unclear, Go to Ops\n\nRachel (patient ops director) ends timing debates with phone data. If Sara is uncertain whether a send window is clean, she escalates to ops before sending. Never guess on visit cadence.\n\n---\n\n### This Week's Checklist for Sara\n\n- [ ] Pull this week's patient appointment calendar before Wednesday send prep\n- [ ] Run suppression check: remove anyone with a visit in the prior 48h\n- [ ] Run bedside test on all subject lines and preview text\n- [ ] Confirm lifecycle tool 48h gate is active (verify in ops)\n- [ ] Flag any copy with clinical outcome language for Maya + James review\n- [ ] Check any content approaching the two-week organic window for paid consideration\n\n---\n\nTwo things worth flagging for your Wednesday partner sync: confirm whether the 48h suppression list is pulling from real-time appointment data or a manual export, and verify whether Sara has visibility into appointment cancellations (a cancelled appointment is still a hard day).       3:This document explains **how the Vibey harness works**, from the moment a user acts in the product down to the database, background workers, and the OpenClaw gateway. It is written to stand alone: you do not need other docs to understand the architecture, though file paths point to code when you need to change behavior.
      12:- **`apps/agent-api`** — chat streaming, OpenClaw proxy, artifact tool execution (`vibey_backend`), agent definition sync, context compaction.
      14:- **`apps/mission-worker`** — BullMQ workers + schedulers that advance **missions** (plan → execute → review) from **database state**.
      15:- **OpenClaw** (in-repo under `apps/openclaw`, deployed with the agent stack) — the **gateway** that runs the embedded agent: sessions, tools, skills, workspace files.
      16:- **Supabase (Postgres + RLS)** — source of truth for users, agents, missions, conversations, skills, definitions, integrations metadata, etc.
      18:The **LLM** only reasons inside OpenClaw. The harness decides **which user and agent** that run belongs to, **what text and context** are passed in, **whether each tool call is legal**, and **how long-running missions move forward** when no one is typing in chat.
      26:1. **Synchronous / conversational** — Studio (or similar) sends messages to **`agent-api`**. The user sees streaming tokens and tool progress. This path is **request-driven**: one HTTP request (often long-lived SSE) per turn.
      27:2. **Structured / asynchronous** — Mission Control (Kanban tasks) mutates **`tasks`** and **`missions`** via **`apps/api`**. The browser does **not** call OpenClaw directly. Instead, **`mission-worker`** notices state in the database and enqueues work. This path is **event- and poll-driven**.
      33:## Part 2 — `agent-api` versus `apps/api`
      37:| Chat turns, streaming UX, OpenClaw `/v1/responses` proxy           | **`agent-api`** | Needs service-role / VM identity, `x-session-key` semantics, and tight coupling to the gateway. |
      39:| Executing `vibey_backend` tool actions                             | **`agent-api`** | **`ArtifactsService.executeAction`** runs here; every action is RBAC-checked.                   |
      41:**Rule of thumb:** if OpenClaw or the artifact tool surface is involved, you are usually in **`agent-api`**. If the UI is doing CRUD on missions/tasks for the Kanban, you are usually in **`apps/api`**.
      45:## Part 3 — Studio chat: one turn from HTTP to OpenClaw
      49:Chat is handled in **`apps/agent-api`** (e.g. `ChatService` + **`OpenClawProxyService`** in `apps/agent-api/src/modules/chat/services/`). The proxy calls the gateway with **`POST /v1/responses`** and **`stream: true`** so the HTTP response is **SSE** (server-sent events), which the service maps into the Studio timeline events (status, tool\_\*, content_delta, done, error). Compaction summarization uses **`POST /v1/chat/completions`** on the same gateway (see `ContextWindowService`).
      55:- **`input`** — an array of **messages** (and similar items) built from recent conversation + optional images. OpenClaw’s gateway merges **system/developer** items into extra system context; **user/assistant** items become the conversational thread the model sees.
      56:- **`instructions`** — a **separate string** merged into OpenClaw’s **extra system prompt** (credentials, IDs, static guardrails). Vibey keeps volatile narrative in user-role content and stable identifiers in `instructions`.
      62:**`OpenClawProxyService`** normalizes gateway SSE into a **small set of client events** (e.g. status, tool_start / tool_update / tool_end, content_delta, error, done). Tool names like **`vibey_backend`** get human-readable labels for the timeline.
      64:### 3.4 Chat session keys (agent-api)
      66:**`AgentRuntimeService`** in **`apps/agent-api/src/modules/shared/agent-runtime.service.ts`** builds the chat session key:
      71:**Gateway agent id for chat** is resolved as: `level === 'system'` → `'vibey'`; **otherwise the literal `agentKey`** (so `copywriter`, `hr`, etc. route to distinct OpenClaw agent ids when configured).
      73:That differs from **mission-worker** routing (below): there, `c_level` and `manager` map to gateway id **`manager`**, and **`employee`** to **`employee`**.
      79:Long threads cannot be sent in full forever. **`ContextWindowService`** (`apps/agent-api/src/modules/chat/services/context-window.service.ts`):
      83:3. When over budget, summarizes **older unsummarized messages** via **`POST /v1/chat/completions`** on the **same OpenClaw gateway** (cheap model), with a structured markdown summary prompt.
      122:- **`addSubtasks`** appends up to 5 new subtasks (with intent packets). Logged as `mission.scope.append_subtasks`. Root subtasks (no deps) are auto-enqueued for execution.
      123:- **`fullReplan`** cancels all non-done subtasks (status → `cancelled`), sets mission to `planning`, and enqueues a new plan job. Logged as `mission.scope.replan`. The plan phase receives `[REPLAN CONTEXT]` with the reason, user comments, and completed subtask summaries.
      129:## Part 6 — Mission-worker: outbox, BullMQ, scheduler
      133:**`MissionsService.processMission`** (`apps/mission-worker/src/modules/missions/services/missions.service.ts`) is a **switch** on `job.data.phase`: **`plan`**, **`execute`**, **`review`**. The worker does not plan work itself; it **calls OpenClaw** with prompts prepared for each phase.
      137:Work is queued by inserting rows into **`mission_outbox`** with `event_type` such as:
      139:- `mission.plan.requested`
      140:- `mission.execute.requested`
      141:- `mission.subtask.execute.requested` (payload includes `subtask_id`)
      142:- `mission.review.requested`
      144:**`MissionsOutboxDispatcherService`** maps each row to a **BullMQ job** (`missions.processor.ts` consumes jobs). Dedupe keys reduce double execution.
      150:- Run **stalled-work detection** for items stuck **`in_progress`** longer than **`missions.stalledMinutes`** (default **10** minutes): it reconstructs the **expected OpenClaw session key** and probes the gateway; if that session is not active, it resets work so BullMQ can retry.
      154:Eligible **subtasks** (`pending` with all `depends_on` done) enqueue **`mission.subtask.execute.requested`** via **`MissionStateRepository.enqueueReadySubtaskEvents`**.
      156:### 6.4 Mission session keys (mission-worker)
      158:**`AgentRuntimeService`** in **`apps/mission-worker/src/modules/missions/services/agent-runtime.service.ts`**:
      169:These keys **isolate OpenClaw sessions** per mission/subtask so parallel missions do not corrupt each other’s tool context.
      171:### 6.5 Calling OpenClaw from missions
      176:- Builds **`input`** as a short scripted thread: optional `[CONTEXT]` user message + assistant ack, then the real task user message — so campaign text lands predictably in the prompt shape OpenClaw expects.
      177:- Uses **non-streaming** Open Responses against **agent-api’s** proxied gateway path (same ecosystem as chat, different consumer).
      197:This string is what becomes `[CONTEXT]` in mission OpenClaw calls.
      203:### 8.1 `vibey_backend`
      205:The OpenClaw tool plugin **`docker/tools/vibey-backend`** registers **`vibey_backend`** with a large **`SUPPORTED_ACTIONS`** list (campaign, ads, funnels, GitHub, missions, memory, integrations, etc.). Descriptions teach the model what exists; **they are not authorization**.
      209:Every tool invocation is **`executeAction(action, data, sessionKey)`** (`apps/agent-api/src/modules/artifacts/services/artifacts.service.ts`):
      245:OpenClaw agents read **workspace files**: `AGENTS.md`, `ROLE.md`, `SOUL.md`, `TOOLS.md`, **`skills/<skill_key>/SKILL.md`**, workflows, etc.
      247:**`AgentSyncService`** (`apps/agent-api/src/modules/agent-sync/services/agent-sync.service.ts`):
      249:1. On startup (when `USER_ID` is a UUID), loads **`agent_definitions`**, **`agent_skills`**, **`agent_skill_resources`**, **`agent_workflows`**, **`agents_registry`** from Supabase (user rows + global templates as designed).
      253:5. Calls **`OpenClawGatewayService.ensureAgent`** so the gateway registers the workspace path and enabled skill ids for that **`agentKey`**.
      263:1. Browser → **`agent-api`** chat endpoint with conversation id, campaign id (optional), agent key.
      266:4. **`OpenClawProxyService`** streams **`/v1/responses`** to the gateway with `input`, `instructions`, `sessionKey`, model.
      267:5. OpenClaw runs the agent; it may call **`vibey_backend`** with an **action** and payload.
      268:6. Gateway forwards to **`agent-api` artifacts** with the same **session key**.
      269:7. **`authorizeAction`** runs; on allow, handler executes against **user-scoped Supabase** (or calls other internal services).
      270:8. Result returns through OpenClaw → SSE → browser.
      274:1. Browser → **`apps/api`** creates/updates **`tasks`** / **`missions`** (and comments → **`missions_logs`**).
      276:3. **`mission_outbox`** gains events; **dispatcher** enqueues **BullMQ** jobs.
      277:4. **`MissionsService`** runs **plan** (manager OpenClaw call) → persists **plan + subtasks** → mission to **`todo`**.
      278:5. Scheduler / outbox enqueue **execute** jobs per ready subtask; **execute** calls OpenClaw for the **employee** session key.
      279:6. Subtasks → **`done`** drive mission to **`review`**; **review** calls OpenClaw for **manager**; approvals → **`done`** and optional **stats** update; rejections re-open execution.
      281:Throughout, **tool calls** from those OpenClaw runs use **mission/subtask session keys**, so **`authorizeAction`** resolves the same **user** and **calling agent** and enforces the same **RBAC**.
      290:- **Stall recovery** — watchdog + outbox stale job cleanup (see **`missions.stalledMinutes`**) prevents missions stuck forever after gateway crashes.

           2	-- ORG RLS POLICIES FOR EXISTING TABLES
           3	-- Adds org member read/write access alongside existing personal policies.

           9	-- Helper function: check if user is active org member
          10	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.is_org_member(p_org_id UUID)
          11	RETURNS BOOLEAN
          12	LANGUAGE sql
          13	STABLE
          14	SECURITY DEFINER
          15	AS $$
          16	  SELECT EXISTS (
          17	    SELECT 1 FROM public.org_members
          18	    WHERE org_id = p_org_id
          19	      AND user_id = auth.uid()
          20	      AND status = 'active'
          21	  )
          22	$$;

          11	/**
          12	 * OrgContextGuard — extracts X-Org-Id from request headers, verifies active membership,
          13	 * and attaches orgId + orgRole to the request.
          14	 *
          15	 * When no X-Org-Id header: personal context (orgId = null, orgRole = null).
          16	 * When X-Org-Id present: verifies user is active member, attaches role.
          17	 *
          18	 * Must run AFTER AuthGuard (needs request.user.id).
          19	 */
          20	@Injectable()
          21	export class OrgContextGuard implements CanActivate {

          29	    const userId = request.user?.id

          44	      .from('org_members')

          46	      .eq('org_id', orgId)
          47	      .eq('user_id', userId)

          50	    if (error) {
          51	      this.logger.error(`Org membership lookup failed: ${error.message}`)
          52	      throw new ForbiddenException('Organization access verification failed')
          53	    }
          54
          55	    if (!membership || membership.status !== 'active') {
          56	      throw new ForbiddenException('You are not an active member of this organization')
          57	    }
          58
          59	    request.orgId = orgId
          60	    request.orgRole = membership.role as OrgRole
          61	    request.orgMemberId = membership.id

          63	      membership.role === 'owner' || membership.ai_data_admin === true
          64
          65	    return true
          66	  }
          67	}

           9	import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core'
          10	import type { OrgRole } from '../services/org-scope.service'
          11
          12	export const ORG_ROLE_KEY = 'requiredOrgRole'
          13
          14	/**
          15	 * Decorator: specify minimum org role required for an endpoint.
          16	 * Only enforced when in org context (X-Org-Id header present).
          17	 * In personal context, this guard passes through.
          18	 *
          19	 * @example @RequireOrgRole('editor')   -- editor, creator, admin, owner can access
          20	 * @example @RequireOrgRole('creator')  -- creator, admin, owner can access
          21	 * @example @RequireOrgRole('admin')    -- admin, owner can access
          22	 * @example @RequireOrgRole('owner')    -- owner only
          23	 */
          24	export const RequireOrgRole = (role: OrgRole) => SetMetadata(ORG_ROLE_KEY, role)
          25
          26	const ORG_ROLE_HIERARCHY: Record<OrgRole, number> = {
          27	  owner: 5,
          28	  admin: 4,
          29	  creator: 3,
          30	  editor: 2,
          31	  viewer: 1,
          32	}
          33
          34	/**
          35	 * OrgRoleGuard — checks if user's org role meets the minimum required by @RequireOrgRole().
          36	 *
          37	 * Must run AFTER AuthGuard + OrgContextGuard (needs request.orgId + request.orgRole).
          38	 *
          39	 * Behavior:
          40	 * - No @RequireOrgRole() decorator: passes through (no role check)
          41	 * - Not in org context (orgId = null): passes through (personal context, no org role needed)
          42	 * - In org context: checks orgRole >= requiredRole
          43	 */
          44	@Injectable()
          45	export class OrgRoleGuard implements CanActivate {
          46	  private readonly logger = new Logger(OrgRoleGuard.name)
          47	  private readonly reflector = new Reflector()
          48
          49	  async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
          50	    const requiredRole = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<OrgRole | undefined>(ORG_ROLE_KEY, [
          51	      context.getHandler(),
          52	      context.getClass(),
          53	    ])
          54
          55	    if (!requiredRole) {
          56	      return true
          57	    }
          58
          59	    const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest()
          60	    const orgId = request.orgId
          61	    const orgRole = request.orgRole as OrgRole | null
          62
          63	    if (!orgId) {
          64	      return true
          65	    }
          66
          67	    if (!orgRole) {
          68	      throw new ForbiddenException('Organization role not resolved')
          69	    }
          70
          71	    const userLevel = ORG_ROLE_HIERARCHY[orgRole]
          72	    const requiredLevel = ORG_ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole]
          73
          74	    if (userLevel < requiredLevel) {
          75	      throw new ForbiddenException(
          76	        `This action requires "${requiredRole}" role. Your role is "${orgRole}".`,
          77	      )
          78	    }
          79
          80	    return true
          81	  }
          82	}

           1	# Mission Privilege Boundaries
           2
           3	## Current Boundary Model
           4
           5	- Request path (`AuthGuard` + `RoleGuard`) uses user-scoped RLS clients.
           6	- `RoleGuard` no longer reads roles with service-role credentials.
           7	- Worker paths keep service-role usage only for machine-to-machine mission processing.
           8	- Outbox RLS remains strict for user inserts and service-role operational updates.
           9
          10	## Approved Service-Role Surfaces
          11
          12	- `apps/mission-worker/src/lib/services/database.service.ts`
          13	- `apps/queue-worker/src/lib/services/database.service.ts`
          14
          15	These are background workers without user JWT context. Service-role usage here is intentional and required.
          16
          17	## Reduced Service-Role Surfaces
          18
          19	- `packages/api-shared/src/guards/role.guard.ts` migrated to request-scoped client from `AuthGuard`.
          20
          21	## Enforcement
          22
          23	- Any new API endpoint must prefer `request.supabase` (RLS-scoped) for user data access.
          24	- Service-role client additions must include a specific machine-only justification.

           1	-- Provider billing attempts keep a durable provider identity before settlement.
           2	-- This lets OpenRouter generations reconcile after interrupted streams or delayed cost indexing.
           3
           4	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.provider_billing_attempts (
           5	  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
           6	  attempt_key TEXT NOT NULL,
           7	  source_app TEXT NOT NULL,
           8	  source_path TEXT NOT NULL,
           9	  billing_owner_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'personal'
          10	    CHECK (billing_owner_type IN ('personal', 'org', 'platform', 'subscription')),
          11	  user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
          12	  org_id UUID REFERENCES public.organizations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
          13	  campaign_id UUID REFERENCES public.campaigns(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
          14	  conversation_id UUID,
          15	  feature TEXT NOT NULL,
          16	  action TEXT,
          17	  service_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text',
          18	  provider TEXT NOT NULL,
          19	  requested_model TEXT,
          20	  resolved_model TEXT,
          21	  provider_generation_id TEXT,
          22	  provider_request_id TEXT,
          23	  input_tokens INTEGER,
          24	  output_tokens INTEGER,
          25	  cache_read_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
          26	  cache_write_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
          27	  total_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
          28	  provider_cost_usd NUMERIC(12,6),
          29	  estimated_cost_usd NUMERIC(12,6),
          30	  final_cost_usd NUMERIC(12,6),
          31	  credits_calculated INTEGER,
          32	  credits_charged INTEGER,
          33	  ai_usage_event_id UUID REFERENCES public.ai_usage_events(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
          34	  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending_provider_id'
          35	    CHECK (
          36	      status IN (
          37	        'pending_provider_id',
          38	        'pending_settlement',
          39	        'settling',
          40	        'settled',
          41	        'no_charge',
          42	        'failed_retryable',
          43	        'unrecoverable',
          44	        'charge_failed'
          45	      )
          46	    ),
          47	  last_error TEXT,
          48	  attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
          49	  next_attempt_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
          50	  locked_by TEXT,
          51	  locked_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
          52	  metadata_json JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
          53	  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
          54	  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
          55	  settled_at TIMESTAMPTZ
          56	);
          57
          58	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS provider_billing_attempts_attempt_key_uidx
          59	  ON public.provider_billing_attempts(attempt_key);
          60
          61	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS provider_billing_attempts_provider_generation_uidx
          62	  ON public.provider_billing_attempts(provider, provider_generation_id)
          63	  WHERE provider_generation_id IS NOT NULL;
          64
          65	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS provider_billing_attempts_status_next_attempt_idx
          66	  ON public.provider_billing_attempts(status, next_attempt_at);
          67
          68	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS provider_billing_attempts_owner_idx
          69	  ON public.provider_billing_attempts(user_id, org_id, created_at DESC);
          70
          71	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS provider_billing_attempts_conversation_idx
          72	  ON public.provider_billing_attempts(conversation_id, created_at DESC);
          73
          74	CREATE TRIGGER update_provider_billing_attempts_updated_at
          75	  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.provider_billing_attempts
          76	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_updated_at_column();
          77
          78	ALTER TABLE public.provider_billing_attempts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
          79
          80	DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "service_role_full" ON public.provider_billing_attempts;
          81	CREATE POLICY "service_role_full" ON public.provider_billing_attempts
          82	  FOR ALL
          83	  USING (auth.role() = 'service_role')
          84	  WITH CHECK (auth.role() = 'service_role');
          85
          86	ALTER TABLE public.ai_usage_events
          87	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS provider_billing_attempt_id UUID
          88	    REFERENCES public.provider_billing_attempts(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
          89	  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS billing_settlement_status TEXT;
          90
          91	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ai_usage_events_provider_billing_attempt_idx
          92	  ON public.ai_usage_events(provider_billing_attempt_id);
          93
          94	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ai_usage_events_billing_settlement_status_idx
          95	  ON public.ai_usage_events(billing_settlement_status);
          96
          97	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.claim_provider_billing_attempts(
          98	  p_limit INTEGER DEFAULT 25,
          99	  p_worker_id TEXT DEFAULT NULL
         100	)
         101	RETURNS SETOF public.provider_billing_attempts
         102	LANGUAGE plpgsql
         103	SECURITY INVOKER
         104	SET search_path = public
         105	AS $$
         106	BEGIN
         107	  IF auth.role() IS DISTINCT FROM 'service_role' THEN
         108	    RETURN;
         109	  END IF;
         110
         111	  RETURN QUERY
         112	  WITH candidates AS (
         113	    SELECT id
         114	    FROM public.provider_billing_attempts
         115	    WHERE (
         116	        status IN ('pending_settlement', 'failed_retryable')
         117	        AND next_attempt_at <= now()
         118	      )
         119	      OR (
         120	        status = 'pending_provider_id'
         121	        AND created_at <= now() - INTERVAL '2 hours'
         122	      )
         123	    ORDER BY next_attempt_at ASC, created_at ASC
         124	    LIMIT GREATEST(1, LEAST(COALESCE(p_limit, 25), 250))
         125	    FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
         126	  )
         127	  UPDATE public.provider_billing_attempts attempt
         128	  SET
         129	    status = 'settling',
         130	    attempts = attempt.attempts + 1,
         131	    locked_by = COALESCE(NULLIF(p_worker_id, ''), 'provider-billing-reconciler'),
         132	    locked_at = now(),
         133	    updated_at = now()
         134	  FROM candidates
         135	  WHERE attempt.id = candidates.id
         136	  RETURNING attempt.*;
         137	END;
         138	$$;
         139
         140	GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.claim_provider_billing_attempts(INTEGER, TEXT) TO service_role;
         141
         142	COMMENT ON TABLE public.provider_billing_attempts IS
         143	  'Durable provider-level billing attempts used to settle exact provider costs after streaming or async completion.';
         144
         145	COMMENT ON COLUMN public.provider_billing_attempts.attempt_key IS
         146	  'Caller-supplied idempotency key for a billable provider attempt.';
         147
         148	COMMENT ON COLUMN public.provider_billing_attempts.provider_generation_id IS
         149	  'Provider generation identifier, for OpenRouter usually x-generation-id or response/body id.';

When the pane is wide enough the card sits in-flow on the right, inset from the chat edges, with no full-height divider; otherwise it drops from the header toggle. Connections, Outputs, Sources, and Tasks stack as collapsible sections (empty ones start closed). The create (+) catalog swaps the card body in place, and meeting-scoped chats list the meeting workspace by name in Connections as a permanent, non-removable row that opens `/home/meetings?meeting=<call item id>`. Space media listeners no longer consume the shared media-open event, so generated-image cards can continue into the persistent shell viewer. 30. Every chat-history row resolves one per-user activity state with fixed priority: amber **Needs your action**, animated purple **Working**, blue **New activity**, then no indicator for read/idle. Opening a conversation records its read timestamp immediately; a background stream that completes while another conversation is selected becomes unread without waiting for a feed refresh. 31. Image viewer **Markup** mode records pen paths and pins as normalized image coordinates. Each mark owns separately saved feedback, remains selectable in the top tool strip, and can be deleted independently. The feedback card can be dragged between canvas corners so it does not obscure the target. **Regenerate with edits** is a separate top-level action and converts all feedback-complete marks into strict location-specific edit instructions before using the existing image-edit stream. The source remains unchanged; the generated result is registered and retained as a new media version in the history rail. 32. Full Home new chat surfaces up to three **Suggested next moves** directly beneath the shared standard chat composer. `GET /api/home/next-moves` reads canonical Meetings `follow_up` Space items and keeps only the signed-in user's own actions plus unassigned follow-ups from meetings they actually attended (calendar invitees, participant emails, Fathom attendee tags, or recording attendees). Teammate-owned follow-ups from other people's calls are excluded, even when those recordings live in a shared org Meetings space. It then excludes per-user snoozed rows and returns source-aware draft prompts. Selecting a suggestion fills the composer for review without sending it. Snooze hides it for seven days, while Dismiss uses the existing Home recommendation dismissal store for a durable hide. 33. Shell page roots and the Simple sidebar use one `h-full` / `min-h-0` / constrained-flex ownership chain. Inbox, meeting pages, and other page bodies own their vertical overflow, while Recents scrolls independently above the pinned account footer. 34. Pixel and other authorized agents can use the read-only `search_conversations` action when a user refers to another chat. The action searches active conversation titles inside the resolved user and organization scope and returns bounded recent user/assistant excerpts, summaries, and conversation ids. It must be attempted before asking the user to reconstruct accessible chat history. 35. Simple chat keeps **Summary** in the conversation title bar top-right in every state. **Show page** sits beside it while the work card is closed, including `/home?conv=` (which has no work-card header). When the page is open beside chat, **Collapse page** lives in that card's header so it can expand over chat. Opening or closing the summary card must not move Summary. `/home` is recorded as **Home**, never as a blank hover-history row. 36. Meeting workspaces derive a deterministic conversation UUID from the meeting item id. Concurrent workspace hydration or start requests therefore upsert the same chat instead of creating parallel Recents rows. Opening a linked meeting also archives any older unlinked conversations with the same user, organization, and meeting metadata; the linked conversation remains active and the archived copies remain recoverable. 37. Navigation between left-sidebar screens is chat-preserving. `ShellWorkspace` resolves the target through `shell-screen-chat.config.ts`: an open drawer conversation is kept, while a dismissible prompt offers the target screen's different remembered chat. An open pane without a conversation starts fresh instead of restoring unrelated history. Conversations are remembered per screen in `vibey.shell.v1`; Space, Campaign, and channel routes retain their existing scoped chat hosts.

Slack webhook messages enter `slack_observation_events` once; a five-minute analysis schedule consumes only events after an exact cursor, while an hourly reconciliation pass catches missed channel messages and expands threads. Empty five-minute intervals make no model call and do not re-analyze prior messages. Public channels are discovered and joined automatically when the installed Slack token includes `channels:join`; newly joined channels are reconciled immediately so historical context enters the ledger. Administrators can exclude channels from observation, and Team → People → Channels reports discovered, joined, observed, excluded, and inaccessible coverage. Private channels remain invite-only in Slack. A new consumer recovers from the oldest stored ledger event, so a provider outage cannot strand evidence outside a moving lookback window. The analyzer examines every non-Ignored human sender in the selected channels, detects Person Brain facts, repeated workflows, unanswered questions, and client-risk signals together, then advances only after the run succeeds. `person_ids` is not a source-sender filter: it restricts Active recipients, Person Brain compounding, and personal-moment outreach. Large windows are processed in bounded 250-message batches rather than silently dropping later channels. The analyzer uses direct Gemini with a strict response schema and low reasoning level, rejects signals without exact source evidence or at least 80% confidence, resolves the finding's subject from that event's sender, registers previously unseen human senders as durable Manage People records, snapshots readable channel/person/time/source-text evidence onto every proposal, and records exact token usage plus provider cost. Unmatched Slack identities default to External unless they match a portal teammate or retain a manual classification. An explicitly enabled managed Person Brain compounds verified facts in Shadow mode because Brain learning is an internal permission, separate from outbound delivery. Findings about external or ignored people remain internal-only Signals and never enter that external person's DM path; when the connected workspace owner maps to an Internal Slack person, Pixel also creates a separate internal follow-up linked to the signal. Operational alerts enter a cooling lifecycle before delivery: client-risk findings wait 15 minutes, unanswered questions wait 30 minutes, workflow/context briefing signals wait 60 minutes, and personal moments wait about 8 minutes before a standalone Active DM. Personal moments stay off the numbered EOD digest path. At eligibility Pixel refreshes the exact source thread and reactions. Resolved findings are dismissed without messaging, unavailable source evidence remains reviewable, and only still-unresolved alerts addressed to an Internal person who is individually Active can be delivered outside quiet hours. Post-call recaps use their separate confirmation flow and remain immediate. Shadow and Off recipients keep reviewable proposals. In Signals, an administrator can add an instruction, optionally save it as a reusable playbook rule, and create one or more internal Shadow drafts. Multiple named internal recipients create a group-DM draft; external and ignored recipients are filtered again before proposal creation and delivery. Disabled is Off; Shadow continues detection and creates reviewable proposals for recipients who are not individually Active. Other Active actions can send an internal message only when both explicit channel/person allowlists exist and the recipient is classified Internal and individually Active. Daily limits, quiet hours, channel scope, recipient/Person Brain allowlists, Flow run history, and the enabled toggle provide the safety controls.

      ./supabase/migrations/20260313120000_widget_pipeline_data_adapters.sql:6:SET content = E'# Data Adapters\n\nThere are three ways to feed data into a widget: internal adapters, integration calls, and pipelines.\n\n## Internal Adapters\n\nFor data that lives inside Vibey (campaigns, tasks, contacts, etc.). The frontend fetches it directly from the database.\n\n```json\n{ "type": "internal", "adapter": "tasks", "params": { "limit": 20 } }\n```\n\nSupported adapters: campaigns, tasks, contacts, analytics, agents, leads, missions, custom_objects, campaign_team, campaign_stripe_overview, campaign_detail, campaign_deliverables, campaign_offers, campaign_avatars.\n\n## Integration Calls\n\nFor a single API call to a connected service (YouTube, Stripe, Slack, Notion, etc.). Use the action slug exactly as returned by discovery.\n\n```json\n{ "type": "integration", "integration": "youtube", "action": "YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_DETAILS", "params": { "part": ["snippet", "statistics"] } }\n```\n\nThe data lands under `/<ACTION_SLUG>` in the data model, so the widget binds to paths like `/YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_DETAILS/items`.\n\n## Pipelines\n\nWhen the user wants a widget that refreshes with live data — like "top 5 videos by views" or "unanswered Slack messages" — a single API call is not enough. You need to chain steps: fetch a list, enrich with details, sort, and limit.\n\nPipelines run server-side every time the widget loads. The user always sees fresh data, with no hardcoded IDs or values baked in from the conversation.\n\nUse a pipeline whenever the user''s request involves ranking, filtering, sorting, or combining data across multiple API calls.\n\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "top_videos",\n  "steps": [\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "youtube",\n      "action": "YOUTUBE_LIST_CHANNEL_VIDEOS",\n      "params": { "channelId": "me", "maxResults": 50 }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "youtube",\n      "action": "YOUTUBE_GET_VIDEO_DETAILS_BATCH",\n      "params": {\n        "id": { "$ref": "steps.0.items[*].id.videoId" },\n        "parts": ["snippet", "statistics"]\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "sort": { "field": "statistics.viewCount", "order": "desc", "numeric": true },\n      "limit": 5\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe widget definition then binds to `/top_videos/items` (the outputKey becomes the root path).\n\n### How steps work\n\nSteps run in order. Each step can be:\n\n- **integration** — calls a connected service (same format as standalone integration calls)\n- **internal** — fetches from a Vibey adapter\n- **transform** — sorts, limits, or filters the previous step''s output\n\n### Referencing previous steps with $ref\n\nLater steps can reference earlier step outputs using `{ "$ref": "steps.N.path" }` in their params.\n\n| Syntax | Meaning |\n|--------|---------|\n| `steps.0` | Entire output of step 0 |\n| `steps.0.items` | The `items` field from step 0 |\n| `steps.0.items[*].id` | Pluck `id` from every element in `items` (produces an array) |\n| `steps.0.items[*].id.videoId` | Pluck nested `id.videoId` from every element |\n\nThe `[*]` wildcard maps over an array — it extracts the given field from each element and returns a flat array. This is how you pass a list of IDs from a listing call into a batch details call.\n\n### Transform operations\n\nTransform steps operate on the previous step''s output. If the output is an object with `items` or `data` arrays, the transform auto-detects and operates on that array.\n\n| Operation | Format | Example |\n|-----------|--------|---------|\n| sort | `{ "field": "path.to.value", "order": "asc"/"desc", "numeric": true/false }` | Sort by view count descending |\n| limit | number | Take first 5 items |\n| filter | `{ "field": "path", "op": "eq"/"gt"/"lt"/"contains"/"exists", "value": ... }` | Keep only items where status = "active" |\n\n### More pipeline examples\n\n**Top 10 Instagram posts by engagement:**\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "top_ig_posts",\n  "steps": [\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "instagram",\n      "action": "INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_MEDIA",\n      "params": { "limit": 50 }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "sort": { "field": "like_count", "order": "desc", "numeric": true },\n      "limit": 10\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n**Active tasks sorted by due date:**\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "active_tasks",\n  "steps": [\n    { "type": "internal", "adapter": "tasks", "params": { "limit": 100 } },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "filter": { "field": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "active" },\n      "sort": { "field": "due_date", "order": "asc" },\n      "limit": 20\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Choosing the right type\n\n- One-shot data from Vibey (tasks, campaigns, contacts) → **internal**\n- One-shot data from a connected service → **integration**\n- Ranked, filtered, or multi-step data from any source → **pipeline**\n\nWhen in doubt, prefer a pipeline — it produces a self-refreshing widget that always shows the latest data without hardcoded values from the conversation.',

           6	 * Initialize Sentry for the OpenClaw gateway process when DSN is set.

           9	export function ensureSentryGatewayInit(): boolean {
          10	  if (gatewaySentryInited) {

          13	  gatewaySentryInited = true;
          14	  const dsn = process.env.SENTRY_DSN?.trim();

          18	  const enabled =
          19	    process.env.SENTRY_ENABLED === "true" ||
          20	    process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" ||
          21	    process.env.OPENCLAW_SENTRY === "true";
          22	  if (!enabled) {
          23	    return false;
          24	  }

          29	    tracesSampleRate: Number(process.env.SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE ?? 1),
          30	    maxValueLength: Number(process.env.SENTRY_MAX_VALUE_LENGTH ?? 100_000),
          31	    sendDefaultPii: false,
          32	  });
          33	  return true;

           1	# Score, analysis, and self-learning (roadmap + as-built)
           2
           3	This document separates **what Vibey does today** about scoring and quality signals from the **longer product vision** discussed for human–agent evaluation loops and prompt adaptation.
           4
           5	---
           6
           7	## 1. Vision (from product direction)
           8
           9	**Goal:** Close the loop between **outcomes**, **structured evaluation**, and **personalized agent configuration**.
          10
          11	Conceptual loop:
          12
          13	1. **Work completes** (mission / subtask reaches review or done).
          14	2. **Automatic analysis** — e.g. a manager or dedicated “scorer” agent produces **scores with dimensions** (quality, spec adherence, tone, completeness).
          15	3. **Human review** — the user rates the same work on their own rubric and leaves comments on tasks.
          16	4. **Reconciliation** — large gaps (e.g. model score 9 vs user 2) become first-class signals.
          17	5. **Aggregation** — daily or weekly rollups per agent, per campaign, per user.
          18	6. **Adaptation** — suggestions or automated updates to **prompts, skills, or policy hints** stored in the database, compiled at runtime into filesystem definitions (same pipeline as `AgentSyncService`).
          19
          20	This is **not** fully implemented as an end-to-end “self-learning” product surface; sections below document **current code** and **intentional gaps**.
          21
          22	---
          23
          24	## 2. As-built today
          25
          26	### 2.1 Manager review and `qualityScore`
          27
          28	During **mission review**, the manager agent returns structured review output. On **approval**, the review phase may call **`scoreAgentAfterMission`** (`apps/mission-worker/src/modules/missions/services/phases/mission-review-phase.service.ts`).
          29
          30	That routine:
          31
          32	- Reads **`agents_registry.stats`** for the mission’s `assigned_agent_key`.
          33	- Takes **`qualityScore`** from the review result (numeric, defaulting toward mid-scale if missing).
          34	- Derives several **rolling stats** (quality, reliability from revision count, initiative, communication, spec adherence, learning rate, execution speed).
          35	- Uses an exponential-style **smooth update** (lerp weighted by how many missions were already scored) so scores stabilize over time.
          36	- Writes back **`agents_registry.stats`** including `missions_scored`, `last_scored_at`, and an **`overall`** aggregate.
          37
          38	**Evidence:** `scoreAgentAfterMission` and its call site after successful approval in the same file.
          39
          40	### 2.2 What this is not (yet)
          41
          42	- **No automatic prompt mutation** from `stats` — registry stats are **telemetry-like aggregates**, not wired in-repo (as of this writing) to rewrite `agent_definitions` or `agent_skills`.
          43	- **No first-class user rubric** — task comments exist (`missions_logs` with `user.comment` per mission architecture doc), but there is no standardized **user scorecard** entity or weekly “diff my prompts” job described in code here.
          44	- **No dedicated scorer agent** in the architecture docs — review is the **manager** agent’s phase, not a separate scoring service.
          45
          46	---
          47
          48	## 3. Target architecture (incremental path)
          49
          50	The following is a **roadmap shape** that matches the harness elsewhere: keep **source of truth in the database**, **enforce policy in agent-api**, **run long jobs in workers**, **sync to disk** for OpenClaw.
          51
          52	### 3.1 Data we would add or formalize
          53
          54	| Piece                                         | Purpose                                                                                   |
          55	| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
          56	| **Per-task or per-mission evaluation record** | Store model scores, human scores, dimensions, free-text rationale, links to deliverables. |
          57	| **Rubric versioning**                         | So scores are comparable over time when criteria change.                                  |
          58	| **Drift flags**                               | When `                                                                                    | model_score - user_score | > threshold`, mark for review or training data. |
          59
          60	### 3.2 Processing
          61
          62	- **Batch job** (nightly/weekly): aggregate evaluations, produce **recommendations** (human-in-the-loop at first).
          63	- Optional **second-pass LLM**: turn deltas + comments into **concrete prompt/skill edits** as diffs for approval.
          64
          65	### 3.3 Application
          66
          67	- Approved changes update **`agent_definitions` / `agent_skills`** (or a dedicated `prompt_variants` table keyed by user + agent).
          68	- **`AgentSyncService`** (or successor) continues to **materialize** files for the gateway.
          69	- **RBAC** unchanged: learning adjusts **instructions**, not **artifact allowlists**, unless product explicitly adds policy learning (high risk; separate design).
          70
          71	### 3.4 Safety boundaries
          72
          73	- **Fail closed on authorization** — never learn “user asked to bypass policy.”
          74	- **Audit trail** — every auto-suggested prompt change should trace to **which evaluations** produced it.
          75	- **Per-user personalization** — align with multi-tenant RLS already used for `agent_skills` and `agent_definitions`.
          76
          77	---
          78
          79	## 4. Relation to the rest of the harness
          80
          81	- **Policy** (`.documentation/agents/agent-rbac-and-team-architecture.md`) remains the hard gate.
          82	- **Orchestration** (`.documentation/mission-control/task-subtask-architecture.md`) remains where **review** runs today and where richer scoring hooks would attach (same phase, or sub-phase).
          83	- **Context** (compaction, campaign, graph) continues to feed **inputs** to any future scorer; it does not replace **evaluation storage**.
          84
          85	---
          86
          87	## 5. Quick reference — files touched by today’s scoring
          88
          89	| File                                                      | Role                                                                        |
          90	| --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
          91	| `apps/mission-worker/.../mission-review-phase.service.ts` | Calls `scoreAgentAfterMission` on approval; updates `agents_registry.stats` |
          92
          93	For the full harness overview, see **`vibey-harness.md`** in this folder.

      documentation/features/spaces-automation.md:21:- One scheduled `observe_slack_team` action powers Pixel Team intelligence. Slack webhook messages enter `slack_observation_events` once; a five-minute analysis schedule consumes only events after an exact cursor, while an hourly reconciliation pass catches missed channel messages and expands threads. Empty five-minute intervals make no model call and do not re-analyze prior messages. Public channels are discovered and joined automatically when the installed Slack token includes `channels:join`; newly joined channels are reconciled immediately so historical context enters the ledger. Administrators can exclude channels from observation, and Team → People → Channels reports discovered, joined, observed, excluded, and inaccessible coverage. Private channels remain invite-only in Slack. A new consumer recovers from the oldest stored ledger event, so a provider outage cannot strand evidence outside a moving lookback window. The analyzer examines every non-Ignored human sender in the selected channels, detects Person Brain facts, repeated workflows, unanswered questions, and client-risk signals together, then advances only after the run succeeds. `person_ids` is not a source-sender filter: it restricts Active recipients, Person Brain compounding, and personal-moment outreach. Large windows are processed in bounded 250-message batches rather than silently dropping later channels. The analyzer uses direct Gemini with a strict response schema and low reasoning level, rejects signals without exact source evidence or at least 80% confidence, resolves the finding's subject from that event's sender, registers previously unseen human senders as durable Manage People records, snapshots readable channel/person/time/source-text evidence onto every proposal, and records exact token usage plus provider cost. Unmatched Slack identities default to External unless they match a portal teammate or retain a manual classification. An explicitly enabled managed Person Brain compounds verified facts in Shadow mode because Brain learning is an internal permission, separate from outbound delivery. Findings about external or ignored people remain internal-only Signals and never enter that external person's DM path; when the connected workspace owner maps to an Internal Slack person, Pixel also creates a separate internal follow-up linked to the signal. Operational alerts enter a cooling lifecycle before delivery: client-risk findings wait 15 minutes, unanswered questions wait 30 minutes, workflow/context briefing signals wait 60 minutes, and personal moments wait about 8 minutes before a standalone Active DM. Personal moments stay off the numbered EOD digest path. At eligibility Pixel refreshes the exact source thread and reactions. Resolved findings are dismissed without messaging, unavailable source evidence remains reviewable, and only still-unresolved alerts addressed to an Internal person who is individually Active can be delivered outside quiet hours. Post-call recaps use their separate confirmation flow and remain immediate. Shadow and Off recipients keep reviewable proposals. In Signals, an administrator can add an instruction, optionally save it as a reusable playbook rule, and create one or more internal Shadow drafts. Multiple named internal recipients create a group-DM draft; external and ignored recipients are filtered again before proposal creation and delivery. Disabled is Off; Shadow continues detection and creates reviewable proposals for recipients who are not individually Active. Other Active actions can send an internal message only when both explicit channel/person allowlists exist and the recipient is classified Internal and individually Active. Daily limits, quiet hours, channel scope, recipient/Person Brain allowlists, Flow run history, and the enabled toggle provide the safety controls.

         186	### Fly.io
         187
         188	Shared CPU is not equivalent to dedicated CPU. Fly says shared and performance vCPUs run on the same physical hardware, but shared vCPUs have a baseline quota of 5 ms per 80 ms period while performance vCPUs get the full 80 ms. A shared-cpu-2x machine gets 10 ms per 80 ms period total, with burst balance behavior.
         189
         190	Source: https://fly.io/docs/machines/cpu-performance/
         191
         192	Fly exposes metrics for CPU utilization, quota balance, throttling, and steal. The docs specifically call out steal as either quota throttling or host competition.
         193
         194	Source: https://fly.io/docs/machines/cpu-performance/
         195
         196	Fly autostop/autostart can keep one or more machines running using `min_machines_running`, but Fly Proxy autostop/autostart starts and stops existing Machines; it does not create new machines. For thousands of per-user Machines in a single app, Fly says the stop loop cannot keep up and recommends one app per user with dynamic routing or app-managed idle shutdown.

         227
         228	Railway services are containers. Services can be persistent/always-running or scheduled jobs. Railway can deploy from GitHub, local directory, or Docker image, and will use a Dockerfile if found.

         230	Source: https://docs.railway.com/services
         231
         232	Railway supports long-running workers and queues. Their own guide recommends a separate always-on worker service for continuous processing, Redis or RabbitMQ for queues, and private networking for service-to-service communication.

         235
         236	Railway private networking creates encrypted WireGuard tunnels and gives services internal `railway.internal` DNS names.

         239
         240	Railway vertical autoscaling scales services up to the vCPU and memory limits of the plan. Horizontal replicas are manual. Public traffic is randomly distributed among replicas in a single region, and Railway currently does not support sticky sessions.

           2
           3	AI Marketing Agency Platform. Each user gets a persistent AI agency that runs their marketing 24/7.

           5	## Stack
           6
           7	- **Frontend:** Next.js 14 + Tailwind CSS + Supabase Realtime
           8	- **Agent Service:** Node.js + OpenClaw-style runtime
           9	- **Database:** Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Auth + Realtime)
          10	- **Infrastructure:** Single VM (Sprint 1) → Pausable microVMs (Sprint 2+)

      supabase/migrations/20260313120000_widget_pipeline_data_adapters.sql:6:SET content = E'# Data Adapters\n\nThere are three ways to feed data into a widget: internal adapters, integration calls, and pipelines.\n\n## Internal Adapters\n\nFor data that lives inside Vibey (campaigns, tasks, contacts, etc.). The frontend fetches it directly from the database.\n\n```json\n{ "type": "internal", "adapter": "tasks", "params": { "limit": 20 } }\n```\n\nSupported adapters: campaigns, tasks, contacts, analytics, agents, leads, missions, custom_objects, campaign_team, campaign_stripe_overview, campaign_detail, campaign_deliverables, campaign_offers, campaign_avatars.\n\n## Integration Calls\n\nFor a single API call to a connected service (YouTube, Stripe, Slack, Notion, etc.). Use the action slug exactly as returned by discovery.\n\n```json\n{ "type": "integration", "integration": "youtube", "action": "YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_DETAILS", "params": { "part": ["snippet", "statistics"] } }\n```\n\nThe data lands under `/<ACTION_SLUG>` in the data model, so the widget binds to paths like `/YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_DETAILS/items`.\n\n## Pipelines\n\nWhen the user wants a widget that refreshes with live data — like "top 5 videos by views" or "unanswered Slack messages" — a single API call is not enough. You need to chain steps: fetch a list, enrich with details, sort, and limit.\n\nPipelines run server-side every time the widget loads. The user always sees fresh data, with no hardcoded IDs or values baked in from the conversation.\n\nUse a pipeline whenever the user''s request involves ranking, filtering, sorting, or combining data across multiple API calls.\n\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "top_videos",\n  "steps": [\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "youtube",\n      "action": "YOUTUBE_LIST_CHANNEL_VIDEOS",\n      "params": { "channelId": "me", "maxResults": 50 }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "youtube",\n      "action": "YOUTUBE_GET_VIDEO_DETAILS_BATCH",\n      "params": {\n        "id": { "$ref": "steps.0.items[*].id.videoId" },\n        "parts": ["snippet", "statistics"]\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "sort": { "field": "statistics.viewCount", "order": "desc", "numeric": true },\n      "limit": 5\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe widget definition then binds to `/top_videos/items` (the outputKey becomes the root path).\n\n### How steps work\n\nSteps run in order. Each step can be:\n\n- **integration** — calls a connected service (same format as standalone integration calls)\n- **internal** — fetches from a Vibey adapter\n- **transform** — sorts, limits, or filters the previous step''s output\n\n### Referencing previous steps with $ref\n\nLater steps can reference earlier step outputs using `{ "$ref": "steps.N.path" }` in their params.\n\n| Syntax | Meaning |\n|--------|---------|\n| `steps.0` | Entire output of step 0 |\n| `steps.0.items` | The `items` field from step 0 |\n| `steps.0.items[*].id` | Pluck `id` from every element in `items` (produces an array) |\n| `steps.0.items[*].id.videoId` | Pluck nested `id.videoId` from every element |\n\nThe `[*]` wildcard maps over an array — it extracts the given field from each element and returns a flat array. This is how you pass a list of IDs from a listing call into a batch details call.\n\n### Transform operations\n\nTransform steps operate on the previous step''s output. If the output is an object with `items` or `data` arrays, the transform auto-detects and operates on that array.\n\n| Operation | Format | Example |\n|-----------|--------|---------|\n| sort | `{ "field": "path.to.value", "order": "asc"/"desc", "numeric": true/false }` | Sort by view count descending |\n| limit | number | Take first 5 items |\n| filter | `{ "field": "path", "op": "eq"/"gt"/"lt"/"contains"/"exists", "value": ... }` | Keep only items where status = "active" |\n\n### More pipeline examples\n\n**Top 10 Instagram posts by engagement:**\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "top_ig_posts",\n  "steps": [\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "instagram",\n      "action": "INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_MEDIA",\n      "params": { "limit": 50 }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "sort": { "field": "like_count", "order": "desc", "numeric": true },\n      "limit": 10\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n**Active tasks sorted by due date:**\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "active_tasks",\n  "steps": [\n    { "type": "internal", "adapter": "tasks", "params": { "limit": 100 } },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "filter": { "field": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "active" },\n      "sort": { "field": "due_date", "order": "asc" },\n      "limit": 20\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Choosing the right type\n\n- One-shot data from Vibey (tasks, campaigns, contacts) → **internal**\n- One-shot data from a connected service → **integration**\n- Ranked, filtered, or multi-step data from any source → **pipeline**\n\nWhen in doubt, prefer a pipeline — it produces a self-refreshing widget that always shows the latest data without hardcoded values from the conversation.',

      supabase/migrations/20260318160000_seed_daily_report_workflow.sql:11:  E'You are running the Daily Report workflow. This produces a complete PDF report of the past 24 hours of campaign performance.\n\nFollow the steps below in order.\n\n## Steps\n\n### Step 1: Identify Campaign\n**Requires input:** Yes\n**Ask user:** "Which campaign should I report on? (Or I can use the campaign you have open.)"\n\nResolve campaign_id from the conversation context or user selection. If no campaign is selected, ask the user to pick one.\n\n### Step 2: Gather 24h Data\n**Requires input:** No\n\nCall `vibey_backend` with action `get_daily_report_data` and data `{"campaign_id":"<resolved>"}` (or omit campaign_id if using session campaign). This returns funnel metrics (visitors, leads, conversion), email metrics (sent, opened, clicked, rates), ad metrics (views, leads, breakdown), Meta insights (if connected), and social activity (created, published, scheduled in last 24h).\n\n### Step 3: Analyze & Synthesize\n**Requires input:** No\n\nInterpret the data. Highlight trends and notable changes. Summarize performance across funnel, email, ads, and social. Identify any gaps or opportunities. Write clear, actionable insights in the user''s voice.\n\n### Step 4: Generate PDF Report\n**Skill:** `pdf-builder` (read `skills/pdf-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** No\n\nFormat the analysis into a report structure. Use `create_pdf` with a clear title (e.g. "Daily Report — [Campaign Name] — [Date]") and markdown content. Include:\n- Executive summary\n- Funnel performance (visitors, leads, conversion rate)\n- Email performance (sent, opened, clicked, rates)\n- Ad performance (views, leads, Meta insights if available)\n- Social activity (posts created, published, scheduled)\n- Key insights and recommendations\n\nUse the brand theme if available for on-brand PDF styling.\n\n---\n\nAfter completing all 4 steps, present the PDF link to the user and offer to run a report for another campaign or time range.',
