      supabase/migrations/20260320223000_brain_memory_routing_skills.sql:34:      || E'If the target layer is ambiguous, return `{ "kind": "blocked", "feedback": "..." }` and ask which layer they want.\n',
      supabase/migrations/20260328200000_rewrite_hr_skills.sql:10:E'# Hiring & Interviews\n\nYour core job is matching what the user needs to the right agent role. Every hire starts with understanding the gap, not jumping to a template.\n\n## The Interview Flow\n\n### Step 1: Understand the Gap\n\nAsk what problem they are trying to solve, not what role they want. Users often know the pain but not the solution.\n\nGood opener: "What''s taking up your time right now that you wish someone else handled?"\n\nListen for signals:\n- Client-facing work (support, onboarding, coaching) -> Support domain\n- Content, ads, social, brand -> Marketing domain\n- Data, reporting, metrics -> Analyst domain\n- Code, integrations, automation -> Developer domain\n- Coordination, planning, oversight -> Management (shared domain)\n\n### Step 2: Match to Domain and Template\n\nThe system has 5 capability domains that determine what an agent can and cannot do:\n\n| Domain | What They Do | RBAC Level |\n|--------|-------------|------------|\n| marketing | Content, ads, funnels, social, brand | Full creative tools |\n| analyst | Data, reporting, metrics, competitive intel | Read-heavy tools |\n| developer | Code, widgets, projects, integrations | Build tools |\n| support | Client-facing conversations, FAQ, coaching | Brain-only, no tools |\n| shared | General, cross-domain, management | Baseline tools |\n\nCheck the ready library first. These templates come with pre-built skills and identity:\n\n**Marketing:** copywriter, designer, media_producer, brand_manager, ads_manager\n**Analyst:** analyst, performance_analyst\n**Developer:** developer, automation_integrations_engineer, qa_engineer, widget_builder\n**Support:** customer_support, customer_success, customer_coach\n**Management:** pm_marketing, pm_product, pm_operations, coach, cfo\n**System:** brain_scholar\n\n### Step 3: Propose the Hire\n\nPresent your recommendation with:\n- Role title and what they''ll handle\n- DISC profile and why it fits (use disc-profiling skill)\n- Suggested name from the template pool or a fresh one\n- Which template to base it on (for skill seeding)\n\n## Creating the Agent\n\nWhen using `create_agent`, always pass `skill_seed_key` matching the closest template. This seeds the agent with the right skills for their domain.\n\nFor support agents specifically, the `skill_seed_key` is critical because it seeds conversation-boundaries, external-user-safety, and the role-specific protocol skill. Without it, the agent has no safety skills for client-facing use.\n\n## Example: Support Hire\n\nUser: "I need someone to handle questions from my coaching clients"\n\n1. Signal: client-facing, coaching -> Support domain\n2. Template match: customer_coach (deep mentoring) or customer_success (onboarding guidance)\n3. Ask: "Are your clients mainly asking questions about the program, or do they need ongoing coaching and accountability?"\n4. If accountability/growth -> customer_coach. If navigation/onboarding -> customer_success. If FAQ/troubleshooting -> customer_support.\n\n## Example: Marketing Hire\n\nUser: "I need help writing my emails and landing pages"\n\n1. Signal: copy, emails, landing pages -> Marketing domain\n2. Template match: copywriter\n3. Propose: "I''d recommend a Senior Conversion Copywriter. They''ll handle your email sequences, landing page copy, and ad scripts. DISC profile I/C — persuasive but precise."',
      supabase/migrations/20260328200000_rewrite_hr_skills.sql:28:E'# Agent Design\n\nEvery agent is defined by three identity files. Together they create a consistent, believable character that users can rely on.\n\n## The Three Identity Files\n\n### SOUL.md — Who the Agent IS\n\nWritten in first person. Defines personality, values, tone, and boundaries.\n\nSections to include:\n- **Who I Am** — 2-3 sentences capturing the agent''s essence and operating philosophy\n- **DISC Profile** — Primary/secondary traits with what they mean in practice (use disc-profiling skill)\n- **Personality & Tone** — 4-5 bullet points defining communication style\n- **Values** — 3 core values with one-sentence explanations\n- **Boundaries** — What the agent will and won''t do\n\nExample excerpt (support agent):\n> I am the problem solver — the one who turns confusion into clarity with the fewest words possible. Warm on the surface, efficient underneath.\n> **Values:** Clarity — the measure of a good answer is whether the user has to ask again. Honesty — trust is built one accurate answer at a time.\n> **Boundaries:** I won''t speculate to seem more helpful. I stay in my lane.\n\nExample excerpt (marketing agent):\n> I am the persuader — words are my medium and conversion is my craft. Every sentence earns the next sentence.\n> **Values:** Impact — copy that doesn''t convert is just words. Craft — every word is chosen, never random.\n> **Boundaries:** I don''t write fluff. If I can''t make it better, I say so.\n\n### ROLE.md — What the Agent DOES\n\nSections to include:\n- **Purpose** — One paragraph on their mission\n- **Responsibilities** — 3-5 numbered responsibility areas (R1, R2, etc.) with 3-4 bullet points each\n- **Core Beliefs** — 3-5 operating principles that guide decisions\n- **Decision Framework** — Numbered steps for how they approach their work\n- **Authority** — Table of what they can and can''t decide\n- **Skills** — Table of capabilities with priority (High/Medium)\n- **Success Metrics** — Output, quality, and behavioral metrics with targets\n\nFor support agents, authority must explicitly state: no promises about the program, no account changes, no financial or legal advice.\n\n### IDENTITY.md — How the Agent PRESENTS\n\nSections to include:\n- **Header** — Role archetype, level, domain, DISC profile, tagline\n- **Communication Style** — Emoji usage, tone descriptor, response length guidance, humor approach\n- **Examples** — 3-4 example messages showing the agent''s voice in action (first message, answering a question, handling uncertainty, redirecting off-topic)\n\n## Design for the Domain\n\n### Support agents (client-facing)\nTone: warm but efficient. Boundaries are critical — explicitly state what the agent won''t do (reveal system internals, speculate, change roles). SOUL.md must include security boundaries. ROLE.md must state zero tool authority.\n\n### Marketing agents\nTone: confident and creative. Focus on craft and conversion. Less about boundaries, more about quality standards.\n\n### Analyst agents\nTone: precise and direct. Numbers first, opinions second. Focus on accuracy and honesty about data limitations.\n\n### Developer agents\nTone: practical and systematic. Focus on reliability and code quality. Less personality, more professionalism.\n\n## Passing Identity to create_agent\n\nWhen creating the agent, pass the content of each file:\n- `soul` parameter -> SOUL.md content\n- `role_content` parameter -> ROLE.md content  \n- `identity` parameter -> IDENTITY.md content\n\nThe system will store these as the agent''s definition files.',

      supabase/migrations/20260311000000_ecology_and_intent_rewrite.sql:23:SET markdown_content = markdown_content || E'\n\n---\n\n## Ecology\n\nFunnels are the conversion layer of the campaign.       supabase/migrations/20260318150100_seed_system_workflows.sql:48:  E'You are running the Launch workflow. This takes an existing campaign and pushes it live.\n\nFollow the steps below in order.       supabase/migrations/20260326200000_support_agent_templates.sql:68:('customer_support', 'support-protocol', 'Support Protocol', 'Structured troubleshooting and response flow for handling client questions. Use whenever a client asks a question, reports a problem, or needs help — this guides you through clarifying the issue, finding the answer in your knowledge, and confirming resolution.', E'# Support Protocol\n\nThis is your structured flow for handling client questions and issues. Following it consistently gives clients a reliable, efficient experience.\n\n## The Flow\n\n### 1. Understand the question\nBefore answering, make sure you understand what the client is actually asking. If the question is ambiguous, ask one clarifying question — not three.\n\n**Example:**\nClient: "How do I get started?"\nYou: "Happy to help! Are you looking for how to access the program materials, or how to begin the first module?"\n\n### 2. Search your knowledge\nLook through your brain content for the relevant answer. If you find it, move to step 3. If not, be honest (see conversation-boundaries skill).\n\n### 3. Deliver a clear answer\nStructure your response for clarity:\n- Lead with the direct answer\n- Add context or steps if needed\n- Keep it concise — respect the client''s time\n\nAvoid walls of text. If the answer is complex, use numbered steps or bullet points.\n\n### 4. Confirm resolution\nEnd with a check: "Does that help?" or "Let me know if you need anything else."\n\nDo not over-ask — one confirmation is enough. If the client moves on, so do you.\n\n## What Makes Good Support\n\n- **Speed**: Answer quickly and directly\n- **Clarity**: No jargon, no ambiguity\n- **Honesty**: Say when you don''t know\n- **Warmth**: Be friendly but not excessive\n\n## Examples\n\n**Good response:**\nClient: "Where do I find the workbook?"\nAgent: "The workbook is in Module 2, under the Resources section. You''ll see a download link at the top of the page. Let me know if you can''t find it!"\n\n**Avoid:**\nClient: "Where do I find the workbook?"\nAgent: "Great question! I''d love to help you with that! So, workbooks are really important for your learning journey. Let me walk you through the entire program structure first..." (too verbose, not answering the question)', '[]'::jsonb, true);

      documentation/features/spaces-automation.md:21:- One scheduled `observe_slack_team` action powers Pixel Team intelligence. Slack webhook messages enter `slack_observation_events` once; a five-minute analysis schedule consumes only events after an exact cursor, while an hourly reconciliation pass catches missed channel messages and expands threads. Empty five-minute intervals make no model call and do not re-analyze prior messages. Public channels are discovered and joined automatically when the installed Slack token includes `channels:join`; newly joined channels are reconciled immediately so historical context enters the ledger. Administrators can exclude channels from observation, and Team → People → Channels reports discovered, joined, observed, excluded, and inaccessible coverage. Private channels remain invite-only in Slack. A new consumer recovers from the oldest stored ledger event, so a provider outage cannot strand evidence outside a moving lookback window. The analyzer examines every non-Ignored human sender in the selected channels, detects Person Brain facts, repeated workflows, unanswered questions, and client-risk signals together, then advances only after the run succeeds. `person_ids` is not a source-sender filter: it restricts Active recipients, Person Brain compounding, and personal-moment outreach. Large windows are processed in bounded 250-message batches rather than silently dropping later channels. The analyzer uses direct Gemini with a strict response schema and low reasoning level, rejects signals without exact source evidence or at least 80% confidence, resolves the finding's subject from that event's sender, registers previously unseen human senders as durable Manage People records, snapshots readable channel/person/time/source-text evidence onto every proposal, and records exact token usage plus provider cost. Unmatched Slack identities default to External unless they match a portal teammate or retain a manual classification. An explicitly enabled managed Person Brain compounds verified facts in Shadow mode because Brain learning is an internal permission, separate from outbound delivery. Findings about external or ignored people remain internal-only Signals and never enter that external person's DM path; when the connected workspace owner maps to an Internal Slack person, Pixel also creates a separate internal follow-up linked to the signal. Operational alerts enter a cooling lifecycle before delivery: client-risk findings wait 15 minutes, unanswered questions wait 30 minutes, workflow/context briefing signals wait 60 minutes, and personal moments wait about 8 minutes before a standalone Active DM. Personal moments stay off the numbered EOD digest path. At eligibility Pixel refreshes the exact source thread and reactions. Resolved findings are dismissed without messaging, unavailable source evidence remains reviewable, and only still-unresolved alerts addressed to an Internal person who is individually Active can be delivered outside quiet hours. Post-call recaps use their separate confirmation flow and remain immediate. Shadow and Off recipients keep reviewable proposals. In Signals, an administrator can add an instruction, optionally save it as a reusable playbook rule, and create one or more internal Shadow drafts. Multiple named internal recipients create a group-DM draft; external and ignored recipients are filtered again before proposal creation and delivery. Disabled is Off; Shadow continues detection and creates reviewable proposals for recipients who are not individually Active. Other Active actions can send an internal message only when both explicit channel/person allowlists exist and the recipient is classified Internal and individually Active. Daily limits, quiet hours, channel scope, recipient/Person Brain allowlists, Flow run history, and the enabled toggle provide the safety controls.
      documentation/features/spaces-automation.md:22:- Operational detection and human briefing selection are separate. Each analysis window can retain up to 40 high-confidence operational findings in `agent_cases`, even when the daily delivery budget is exhausted; only the later delivery selector ranks the small set worth messaging now. The ledger rolls up by Company → Clients Program → client campaign container → campaign Space without copying a case between scopes. Slack asks use the mapped channel/client campaign; Page Grader QC, Proactive Launch, and Campaign QC findings use their explicit client/campaign metadata; proposed post-call follow-ups use their call-item and Space identity; and accepted Pixel offers use the same case contract. Post-call cases remain open during Shadow/admin review and resolve only after confirmation or explicit automatic delivery. EOD processing first refreshes every due Slack source thread and nearby channel replies, then builds the update from still-open cases. Direct channel answers from an explicitly mentioned teammate, plus the first adjacent answer to an unmentioned question, resolve the ask without requiring a Slack thread. Composite status recaps containing completed or live work are not stored as one open commitment. Unanswered asks receive a hard 24-hour due time and create one owner escalation when breached. The EOD composer receives the exact local date, must preserve explicit live/completed/pending status, rejects future language attached to past dates, and fails over to deterministic evidence copy when it produces vague roadmap language. Page Grader acknowledge, snooze, and resolve buttons update the same case row; confirmed post-call work and completed offers resolve their cases.

      documentation/features/missions.md:37:The **Client Lifecycle** playbook is the guided agency operating path from onboarding through ongoing optimization. It first audits the selected client's Client Brain and live campaign context against Company Brain methodology, then stops for human confirmation before treating onboarding context as authoritative. It reuses existing Avatar and Offer records, requires approval of their exact ids before strategy, binds those ids into canonical campaign context, produces the client strategy and campaign roadmap, and asks the operator which existing production playbooks to launch as child Missions. After that approval, a deterministic Canvas stage reads the current campaign revision and converts the approved roadmap into connected stages, canonical resource cards, and actionable placeholders without replacing unrelated Canvas work. Launch readiness then reconciles child Mission deliverables, native Space tasks, campaign Canvas, and Page Grader Work Requests as distinct canonical records before explicit launch authorization. The lifecycle finishes with an optimization cadence. Later Mission steps and normal client chat both filter Offer and Avatar context through those approved ids instead of silently selecting recent or first-available records; unresolved approved ids remain visible as unresolved and never fall back to another record. Client chat injects this canonical campaign asset block alongside Theme and Brain context, so direct conversation and Mission execution share the same campaign fundamentals. Mission execution also sends the current step request and campaign id through the same Brain retrieval path used by chat, so automatic Client/Campaign Brain and Company Brain grounding is scoped to the work being performed. The playbook never duplicates Avatar or Offer records and never publishes, spends, or sends messages without its human gates. It is available both from the canonical Create > Mission catalog and directly under Create > More, while conversational lifecycle requests use the same playbook id and source-conversation contract.
      documentation/features/missions.md:163:- Campaign context (`campaign_id`) remains agent/reporting context and is not automatically the sharing boundary.
      documentation/features/missions.md:180:- **Webinar pre-call-first lifecycle**: every new Webinar Fulfillment mission runs the complete flow beginning with Atlas context preparation and Reed's pre-call strategy map. After the human confirms the call happened, Atlas automatically lists connected Fathom meetings and ranks candidates by calendar invitee email/domain, invitee names, title/topic, scheduled or recording time, and transcript mentions. The user does not need to choose from a recording picker; Atlas asks for one distinguishing detail or direct link only when the best candidates remain genuinely tied. Kickoff transcripts, call links, and research enrich the flow but cannot skip pre-call work; legacy `start_at` values are ignored.
      documentation/features/missions.md:187:- **Meta Ads Audit & Optimization playbook**: Missions can start a dedicated Blaze-owned audit that verifies the client and actual success event, compares live objective-specific performance, produces prioritized recommendations with exact object IDs and guardrails, and stops at a human approval gate. The cycle can remain recommendation-only or apply a bounded approved set through native or Composio Meta, never activate paused objects, and then verify the resulting state and next measurement window.

Automatic pattern-analysis events are debounced for five minutes, coalesced per Brain, and held to one active pass at a time; an explicit manual analysis bypasses the debounce. Image edits use the multimodal image route for GPT and Gemini, support one or more reference images, preserve the source ratio (including 4:5 static ads), expose Square / Portrait ad / Portrait / Story / Landscape / Widescreen actions in the top toolbar, and save every edit back to the source conversation. The editor keeps a fixed, scrollable conversation timeline with the selected version highlighted, fits tall images inside the viewport, and provides a floating prompt composer with reference uploads and voice transcription. It downloads the actual file, exposes **Add to chat** as a direct action that attaches the selected version without dismissing the studio, and keeps **Open in new tab** / **Open in Canva** in the overflow menu. Opening or browsing media never attaches it automatically. 14. `/artifacts` is the account-wide artifact library. It paginates through docs and media, merges every campaign-artifact family from the active organization plus personal legacy assets owned by the signed-in user, labels each row with its campaign or Space, and opens rows in the shared viewer. Uploaded assets are hidden by default and available through the source filter. Type filters include Docs, Images, Videos, Sheets, Presentations, Funnels, Campaign assets, and Files. Video rows and cards render a muted first-frame preview and open in the shared video viewer. More → Artifacts links here; Space-specific views remain inside their Space. 15. Forking an assistant turn creates a new conversation with the original messages through that turn, adds it to chat state, and navigates to the canonical `/home?conv=` URL for the returned fork id. The success toast is shown only after creation succeeds. 16. Every shared Chat composer can attach a person from the `@` menu or the plus menu. **People** combines active portal teammates with Slack-only managed people in the active organization. The server validates the selected identity, resolves its managed Person Brain or canonical User Brain, and adds that durable person context to the agent turn. The Home composer loads People even when no campaign is selected. 17. Home / New chat uses the standard composer with an inset shelf beneath it for Choose Space and Plugins only — no Try-tip banner and no Mission/Offer/artifact chips above the input. Active chats show a rotating idle Try-tip catalog above the composer; closing a tip hides the banner in that chat. Create actions stay in the + Create menu; selecting one still seeds the visible request and attaches a hidden routing contract that names the matching read/write actions, requires a successful tool receipt before claiming completion, and remains active only while the seeded request prefix is intact. 18. Home layout preference version 3 re-seeds old local and server layouts once to full-width Agenda + a two-row-tall Inbox. Customize mode supports independent 1/2-column width and 1/2/3-row height controls for every card, and the Home canvas scrolls through the full configured layout. Users can still customize the dashboard and add the lazy-loaded Ask Pixel composer. 19. Inbox reads `user_notifications` through the dedicated missions-notifications controller. `inbox_bucket`, `snoozed_until`, and `cleared_at` stay independent from `read_at`; one RPC returns unread counts for Primary / Other / Later / Cleared. Inserts are classified by type, realtime inserts use the same client predicate, and clear/snooze/move/read actions update optimistically with rollback. Automated import, sync, and completion notices are projected into a separate **System** lane instead of competing with work that needs a decision; the Primary count excludes that virtual lane. 20. Inbox, Meetings, and All Tasks use full-page presentations on their dedicated routes. Inbox uses a responsive list/detail workspace: selecting a row marks it read and keeps its full context plus triage actions visible at the top, approval notices resolve their source mission's current status, and stale approvals are labeled **Resolved**. Native task details replace the current right-side work page rather than opening over AI Chat; **View source** still navigates to the originating Space, Mission Control item, DM, or integration. Search, mark-all-read, and clear-current-view actions support fast queue triage. Shared selectors render the selected label instead of an empty native-looking control, Inbox dates reserve a stable column so rows align, and chevrons remain vertically centered with their rows. All Tasks keeps the rollup list mounted and opens canonical task detail in a right-side panel. It defaults to every open task, with an Assigned to me filter rather than a My Tasks screen. `/home/my-tasks` redirects there. Expanding the Home dashboard My Tasks card opens All Tasks filtered to assigned work instead of a separate overlay. 21. Chat-history filters render in a body portal so shell flyouts cannot cover or clip them. The Chats and Tasks work page opens a selected conversation in the left drawer without navigating back to Home or closing the work page. 22. Team agent detail uses the canonical AI Chat drawer instead of rendering a second agent-chat runtime. Entering an agent selects that agent, opens a blank canonical chat, expands the history rail, filters history to that agent, and keeps the Team surface attached as visible removable context. The full agent grid remains in the work area while the selected agent profile opens in its right-side detail panel. 23. The page expand/contract control renders only when chat has actually created a collapsible page relationship or the page is currently hidden. A full-page Home conversation has no close-chat action; navigation happens through New chat, history, and the shell destinations. The outer work-area wrapper is the only reveal-transition owner: it clips one right-anchored page surface, while the inner page has no second transform or animation. 24. Campaign/Space attachment is edited in Connections, Recents Filter, and Choose Space. The composer does not show a removable context chip for that attachment. My Tasks uses the shared leading-icon input geometry so the search icon and placeholder never overlap. 25. The default Pixel empty state shows only Pixel's name and capabilities; it does not render an organization-role subtitle. The agent picker keeps Pixel first, followed by a labeled **Other agents** section. 26. Selecting a history row writes that exact conversation into the canonical chat store before opening the drawer. In Simple mode, every history row routes to the full `/home?conv=` chat from any current page instead of opening the legacy drawer in place. The mounted chat panel waits until the selected row is resolvable, merges it into its local list, and then selects the conversation and its saved agent. The shell artifact-viewer adapter remains mounted while hidden so image-open events from either the inline preview or output card can create the first viewer target. On a desktop full-Home conversation, that target opens as a constrained third column beside chat and temporarily replaces Outputs / Sources / Tasks; on ordinary page workspaces and mobile, it temporarily replaces the page work area. Closing it restores the same page state and reopens the conversation summary. Remembered work surfaces carry identifying query params (`conv`, `meeting`, `space`) while transient `chat`/`surface` params are dropped; meeting restores use `/home/meetings?meeting=` and resolve from the in-flight payload or agenda cache. 27. Empty chats render agent selection once in the centered identity. Its chevron appears on hover and opens the agent roster. Established conversations retain the header picker because the centered identity is no longer present. The full Chats and Tasks page aligns its compact heading with the conversation list and shows updated dates plus row dividers without an extra rule beneath the page header. 28. Established chat composers place the model selector beside the voice/send controls and render context usage as a compact segmented line beneath send. New, conversation-less composers omit the meter entirely so context chrome appears only after a chat has started. 29. The work summary uses the same rounded overlay card on every width. When the pane is wide enough the card sits in-flow on the right, inset from the chat edges, with no full-height divider; otherwise it drops from the header toggle. Connections, Outputs, Sources, and Tasks stack as collapsible sections (empty ones start closed). The create (+) catalog swaps the card body in place, and meeting-scoped chats list the meeting workspace by name in Connections as a permanent, non-removable row that opens `/home/meetings?meeting=<call item id>`. Space media listeners no longer consume the shared media-open event, so generated-image cards can continue into the persistent shell viewer. 30. Every chat-history row resolves one per-user activity state with fixed priority: amber **Needs your action**, animated purple **Working**, blue **New activity**, then no indicator for read/idle. Opening a conversation records its read timestamp immediately; a background stream that completes while another conversation is selected becomes unread without waiting for a feed refresh. 31. Image viewer **Markup** mode records pen paths and pins as normalized image coordinates. Each mark owns separately saved feedback, remains selectable in the top tool strip, and can be deleted independently. The feedback card can be dragged between canvas corners so it does not obscure the target. **Regenerate with edits** is a separate top-level action and converts all feedback-complete marks into strict location-specific edit instructions before using the existing image-edit stream. The source remains unchanged; the generated result is registered and retained as a new media version in the history rail. 32. Full Home new chat surfaces up to three **Suggested next moves** directly beneath the shared standard chat composer. `GET /api/home/next-moves` reads canonical Meetings `follow_up` Space items and keeps only the signed-in user's own actions plus unassigned follow-ups from meetings they actually attended (calendar invitees, participant emails, Fathom attendee tags, or recording attendees). Teammate-owned follow-ups from other people's calls are excluded, even when those recordings live in a shared org Meetings space. It then excludes per-user snoozed rows and returns source-aware draft prompts. Selecting a suggestion fills the composer for review without sending it. Snooze hides it for seven days, while Dismiss uses the existing Home recommendation dismissal store for a durable hide. 33. Shell page roots and the Simple sidebar use one `h-full` / `min-h-0` / constrained-flex ownership chain. Inbox, meeting pages, and other page bodies own their vertical overflow, while Recents scrolls independently above the pinned account footer. 34. Pixel and other authorized agents can use the read-only `search_conversations` action when a user refers to another chat. The action searches active conversation titles inside the resolved user and organization scope and returns bounded recent user/assistant excerpts, summaries, and conversation ids. It must be attempted before asking the user to reconstruct accessible chat history. 35. Simple chat keeps **Summary** in the conversation title bar top-right in every state. **Show page** sits beside it while the work card is closed, including `/home?conv=` (which has no work-card header). When the page is open beside chat, **Collapse page** lives in that card's header so it can expand over chat. Opening or closing the summary card must not move Summary. `/home` is recorded as **Home**, never as a blank hover-history row. 36. Meeting workspaces derive a deterministic conversation UUID from the meeting item id. Concurrent workspace hydration or start requests therefore upsert the same chat instead of creating parallel Recents rows. Opening a linked meeting also archives any older unlinked conversations with the same user, organization, and meeting metadata; the linked conversation remains active and the archived copies remain recoverable. 37. Navigation between left-sidebar screens is chat-preserving. `ShellWorkspace` resolves the target through `shell-screen-chat.config.ts`: an open drawer conversation is kept, while a dismissible prompt offers the target screen's different remembered chat. An open pane without a conversation starts fresh instead of restoring unrelated history. Conversations are remembered per screen in `vibey.shell.v1`; Space, Campaign, and channel routes retain their existing scoped chat hosts.

      supabase/migrations/20260311000000_ecology_and_intent_rewrite.sql:23:SET markdown_content = markdown_content || E'\n\n---\n\n## Ecology\n\nFunnels are the conversion layer of the campaign. They sit between traffic sources (ads) and backend systems (email sequences):\n\n- **Depends on:** theme-builder (colors, fonts, voice), offer-builder (headlines, benefits, proof), avatar-builder (pain points, language), ad-builder (traffic destination)\n- **Feeds into:** email-sequence-builder (funnel opt-in triggers welcome/nurture sequences), lead-magnet-builder (the opt-in incentive lives on the funnel page)\n- **Connected to:** meta-publisher (ad destination URLs point to funnel pages), social-content-builder (organic traffic to funnel)\n\nA funnel without an offer produces generic copy. A funnel without a theme looks like a template. A funnel without an email sequence captures leads that go nowhere.',
      supabase/migrations/20260311000000_ecology_and_intent_rewrite.sql:52:| OUTCOME_LEADS | Collect emails, phone numbers, bookings | Lead form submissions, conversions |
      supabase/migrations/20260311000000_ecology_and_intent_rewrite.sql:142:SET markdown_content = markdown_content || E'\n\n---\n\n## Ecology\n\nEmail sequences are the nurture layer that turns leads into customers:\n\n- **Depends on:** offer-builder (benefits, objections, and CTA drive email content), avatar-builder (pain language, desires, and voice), funnel-builder (the opt-in page promise determines what email 1 delivers), lead-magnet-builder (email 1 typically delivers the lead magnet)\n- **Feeds into:** The email sequence is the bridge between the funnel opt-in and the offer pitch. It builds trust, delivers value, and overcomes objections over time.\n- **Connected to:** theme-builder (brand voice carries through email tone)\n\nA sequence disconnected from the offer sounds generic. A sequence that doesn''t reference the lead magnet promise breaks trust immediately. The strongest sequences create a tight narrative arc from ''I just opted in'' to ''I''m ready to buy''.',
      supabase/migrations/20260311000000_ecology_and_intent_rewrite.sql:182:SET markdown_content = markdown_content || E'\n\n---\n\n## Ecology\n\nWebsites are the multi-page brand presence, distinct from single-page funnels:\n\n- **Depends on:** theme-builder (consistent branding across all pages), offer-builder (service/product information for content)\n- **Feeds into:** funnel-builder (website pages can link to dedicated funnel landing pages for specific conversions), email-sequence-builder (contact page leads trigger sequences)\n- **Connected to:** social-content-builder (organic content drives traffic to website), ad-builder (ads can point to website pages)\n\nA website without a theme looks inconsistent across pages. A website without offer data produces generic service descriptions. The contact page must include a data-vibey-capture form to connect with the email system.',
      supabase/migrations/20260310231000_skill_quality_improvements.sql:226:> Use this skill when the user wants to create a downloadable resource: PDF guide, checklist, cheat sheet, workbook, or any gated content used to capture leads.
      supabase/migrations/20260311152000_rewrite_widget_builder_skill_to_json_catalog.sql:45:- leads
      supabase/migrations/20260311152000_rewrite_widget_builder_skill_to_json_catalog.sql:164:- leads
      supabase/migrations/20260313120000_widget_pipeline_data_adapters.sql:6:SET content = E'# Data Adapters\n\nThere are three ways to feed data into a widget: internal adapters, integration calls, and pipelines.\n\n## Internal Adapters\n\nFor data that lives inside Vibey (campaigns, tasks, contacts, etc.). The frontend fetches it directly from the database.\n\n```json\n{ "type": "internal", "adapter": "tasks", "params": { "limit": 20 } }\n```\n\nSupported adapters: campaigns, tasks, contacts, analytics, agents, leads, missions, custom_objects, campaign_team, campaign_stripe_overview, campaign_detail, campaign_deliverables, campaign_offers, campaign_avatars.\n\n## Integration Calls\n\nFor a single API call to a connected service (YouTube, Stripe, Slack, Notion, etc.). Use the action slug exactly as returned by discovery.\n\n```json\n{ "type": "integration", "integration": "youtube", "action": "YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_DETAILS", "params": { "part": ["snippet", "statistics"] } }\n```\n\nThe data lands under `/<ACTION_SLUG>` in the data model, so the widget binds to paths like `/YOUTUBE_GET_CHANNEL_DETAILS/items`.\n\n## Pipelines\n\nWhen the user wants a widget that refreshes with live data — like "top 5 videos by views" or "unanswered Slack messages" — a single API call is not enough. You need to chain steps: fetch a list, enrich with details, sort, and limit.\n\nPipelines run server-side every time the widget loads. The user always sees fresh data, with no hardcoded IDs or values baked in from the conversation.\n\nUse a pipeline whenever the user''s request involves ranking, filtering, sorting, or combining data across multiple API calls.\n\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "top_videos",\n  "steps": [\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "youtube",\n      "action": "YOUTUBE_LIST_CHANNEL_VIDEOS",\n      "params": { "channelId": "me", "maxResults": 50 }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "youtube",\n      "action": "YOUTUBE_GET_VIDEO_DETAILS_BATCH",\n      "params": {\n        "id": { "$ref": "steps.0.items[*].id.videoId" },\n        "parts": ["snippet", "statistics"]\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "sort": { "field": "statistics.viewCount", "order": "desc", "numeric": true },\n      "limit": 5\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe widget definition then binds to `/top_videos/items` (the outputKey becomes the root path).\n\n### How steps work\n\nSteps run in order. Each step can be:\n\n- **integration** — calls a connected service (same format as standalone integration calls)\n- **internal** — fetches from a Vibey adapter\n- **transform** — sorts, limits, or filters the previous step''s output\n\n### Referencing previous steps with $ref\n\nLater steps can reference earlier step outputs using `{ "$ref": "steps.N.path" }` in their params.\n\n| Syntax | Meaning |\n|--------|---------|\n| `steps.0` | Entire output of step 0 |\n| `steps.0.items` | The `items` field from step 0 |\n| `steps.0.items[*].id` | Pluck `id` from every element in `items` (produces an array) |\n| `steps.0.items[*].id.videoId` | Pluck nested `id.videoId` from every element |\n\nThe `[*]` wildcard maps over an array — it extracts the given field from each element and returns a flat array. This is how you pass a list of IDs from a listing call into a batch details call.\n\n### Transform operations\n\nTransform steps operate on the previous step''s output. If the output is an object with `items` or `data` arrays, the transform auto-detects and operates on that array.\n\n| Operation | Format | Example |\n|-----------|--------|---------|\n| sort | `{ "field": "path.to.value", "order": "asc"/"desc", "numeric": true/false }` | Sort by view count descending |\n| limit | number | Take first 5 items |\n| filter | `{ "field": "path", "op": "eq"/"gt"/"lt"/"contains"/"exists", "value": ... }` | Keep only items where status = "active" |\n\n### More pipeline examples\n\n**Top 10 Instagram posts by engagement:**\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "top_ig_posts",\n  "steps": [\n    {\n      "type": "integration",\n      "integration": "instagram",\n      "action": "INSTAGRAM_GET_IG_USER_MEDIA",\n      "params": { "limit": 50 }\n    },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "sort": { "field": "like_count", "order": "desc", "numeric": true },\n      "limit": 10\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n**Active tasks sorted by due date:**\n```json\n{\n  "type": "pipeline",\n  "outputKey": "active_tasks",\n  "steps": [\n    { "type": "internal", "adapter": "tasks", "params": { "limit": 100 } },\n    {\n      "type": "transform",\n      "filter": { "field": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "active" },\n      "sort": { "field": "due_date", "order": "asc" },\n      "limit": 20\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Choosing the right type\n\n- One-shot data from Vibey (tasks, campaigns, contacts) → **internal**\n- One-shot data from a connected service → **integration**\n- Ranked, filtered, or multi-step data from any source → **pipeline**\n\nWhen in doubt, prefer a pipeline — it produces a self-refreshing widget that always shows the latest data without hardcoded values from the conversation.',
      supabase/migrations/20260318150100_seed_system_workflows.sql:28:  E'You are running the Campaign Builder workflow. This builds a complete marketing campaign.\n\nIMPORTANT: Before starting each step, check if the asset already exists in this campaign (use `vibey_backend` list actions). If it does, show the user what exists and ask if they want to use it or rebuild it. Skip steps where assets already exist unless the user wants to redo them.\n\nBetween each step, give the user a progress update: "Step X/7 complete. [Asset] created. Moving to [next step]..."\n\nFollow the steps below in order. For each step, read the referenced skill file before executing.\n\n## Steps\n\n### Step 1: Craft Your Offer\n**Skill:** `offer-builder` (read `skills/offer-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** Yes\n**Ask user:** "Let''s start with what you sell. What''s your product or service, and what problem does it solve?"\n\n5-step offer pipeline — skip if offer already exists in this campaign.\n\n### Step 2: Discover Your Audience\n**Skill:** `avatar-builder` (read `skills/avatar-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** No\n\nBuild buyer persona from the offer — skip if avatar already exists in this campaign.\n\n### Step 3: Set Up Brand Identity\n**Skill:** `theme-builder` (read `skills/theme-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** Yes\n**Ask user:** "Offer and audience are set. Do you have a website I can pull your brand from, or should I design it from scratch?"\n\nDefine colors, fonts, voice — skip if theme already exists in this campaign.\n\n### Step 4: Create Lead Magnet\n**Skill:** `lead-magnet-builder` (read `skills/lead-magnet-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** Yes\n**Ask user:** "What type of free resource would attract your audience? (guide, checklist, cheat sheet, workbook, case study, toolkit)"\n\nCreate a downloadable lead magnet that showcases expertise and captures leads.\n\n### Step 5: Build Landing Page & Funnel\n**Skill:** `funnel-builder` (read `skills/funnel-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** Yes\n**Ask user:** "What kind of page do you need? (opt-in page for the lead magnet, full sales page, webinar registration, or product page)"\n\nBuild a high-converting landing page with the theme, offer copy, and lead magnet integration.\n\n### Step 6: Write Email Sequence\n**Skill:** `email-sequence-builder` (read `skills/email-sequence-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** Yes\n**Ask user:** "What should happen after someone opts in? (welcome + nurture series, launch sequence, or post-purchase flow)"\n\nCreate automated email sequence that nurtures leads from the funnel.\n\n### Step 7: Create Social Content\n**Skill:** `social-content-builder` (read `skills/social-content-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** No\n\nCreate exactly 4 posts — 2 for LinkedIn and 2 for Instagram. The LinkedIn posts should be professional/educational, the Instagram posts should be visual/engaging. All 4 should promote the campaign assets (offer, funnel, lead magnet) using the avatar''s language and pain points, styled with the brand voice from the theme.\n\n---\n\nAfter all 7 steps, present a campaign summary showing every asset created with links/previews.       supabase/migrations/20260318160000_seed_daily_report_workflow.sql:11:  E'You are running the Daily Report workflow. This produces a complete PDF report of the past 24 hours of campaign performance.\n\nFollow the steps below in order.\n\n## Steps\n\n### Step 1: Identify Campaign\n**Requires input:** Yes\n**Ask user:** "Which campaign should I report on? (Or I can use the campaign you have open.)"\n\nResolve campaign_id from the conversation context or user selection. If no campaign is selected, ask the user to pick one.\n\n### Step 2: Gather 24h Data\n**Requires input:** No\n\nCall `vibey_backend` with action `get_daily_report_data` and data `{"campaign_id":"<resolved>"}` (or omit campaign_id if using session campaign). This returns funnel metrics (visitors, leads, conversion), email metrics (sent, opened, clicked, rates), ad metrics (views, leads, breakdown), Meta insights (if connected), and social activity (created, published, scheduled in last 24h).\n\n### Step 3: Analyze & Synthesize\n**Requires input:** No\n\nInterpret the data. Highlight trends and notable changes. Summarize performance across funnel, email, ads, and social. Identify any gaps or opportunities. Write clear, actionable insights in the user''s voice.\n\n### Step 4: Generate PDF Report\n**Skill:** `pdf-builder` (read `skills/pdf-builder/SKILL.md`)\n**Requires input:** No\n\nFormat the analysis into a report structure. Use `create_pdf` with a clear title (e.g. "Daily Report — [Campaign Name] — [Date]") and markdown content. Include:\n- Executive summary\n- Funnel performance (visitors, leads, conversion rate)\n- Email performance (sent, opened, clicked, rates)\n- Ad performance (views, leads, Meta insights if available)\n- Social activity (posts created, published, scheduled)\n- Key insights and recommendations\n\nUse the brand theme if available for on-brand PDF styling.\n\n---\n\nAfter completing all 4 steps, present the PDF link to the user and offer to run a report for another campaign or time range.',

         195	        .triggerAgentSkillsSync(userId, recommendation.target_agent_key, orgId)
         196	        .catch(() => undefined)
         197	      return
         198	    }
         199	    if (recommendation.proposal_kind === 'agent_file_update') {
         200	      await this.applyAgentFile(supabase, userId, orgId, recommendation)
         201	      return
         202	    }
         203	    throw new BadRequestException('Unsupported learning-loop proposal kind')
         204	  }

         337	        recommendation.artifact_lock_key ??
         338	        [orgId, recommendation.target_agent_key, recommendation.target_artifact_kind, recommendation.skill_key].join(':'),
         339	      status: 'running',

         341	      current_metrics: {},

         360	  private metricsFromEvents(
         361	    events: Array<Record<string, unknown>>,
         362	    feedbackSummary: unknown = null,
         363	  ): AgentLearningExperimentMetrics {
         364	    const qualifyingEvents = events.length
         365	    const feedback = this.feedbackSummary(feedbackSummary)
         366	    const negativeFeedbackRate =
         367	      feedback.total_count > 0 ? feedback.negative_count / feedback.total_count : 0
         368	    if (qualifyingEvents === 0) {
         369	      return {
         370	        primarySuccessRate: 0,
         371	        toolErrorRate: 0,
         372	        roleViolationRate: 0,
         373	        negativeFeedbackRate,
         374	      }
         375	    }
         376	    const completed = events.filter((event) => event.status === 'completed').length
         377	    const failed = events.filter((event) => event.status === 'failed').length
         378	    return {
         379	      primarySuccessRate: completed / qualifyingEvents,
         380	      toolErrorRate: failed / qualifyingEvents,
         381	      roleViolationRate: 0,
         382	      negativeFeedbackRate,
         383	    }
         384	  }
         385
         386	  private feedbackSummary(value: unknown): AgentTurnFeedbackSummary {
         387	    const record = this.record(value)
         388	    return {
         389	      total_count: this.numberValue(record.total_count, 0),
         390	      positive_count: this.numberValue(record.positive_count, 0),
         391	      negative_count: this.numberValue(record.negative_count, 0),
         392	      trusted_negative_count: this.numberValue(record.trusted_negative_count, 0),
         393	      top_tags: Array.isArray(record.top_tags)
         394	        ? record.top_tags.filter((tag): tag is string => typeof tag === 'string')
         395	        : [],
         396	    }
         397	  }
         398
         399	  private metricsFromRecord(value: unknown): AgentLearningExperimentMetrics {
         400	    const record = this.record(value)
         401	    return {
         402	      primarySuccessRate: this.numberValue(record.primarySuccessRate, 0.5),
         403	      toolErrorRate: this.numberValue(record.toolErrorRate, 0.1),
         404	      roleViolationRate: this.numberValue(record.roleViolationRate, 0),
         405	      negativeFeedbackRate: this.numberValue(record.negativeFeedbackRate, 0),
         406	    }
         407	  }
         408
         409	  private resourcesFromPatch(
         410	    value: unknown,
         411	    fallback: SkillRecommendationResource[],
         412	  ): SkillRecommendationResource[] {
         413	    const rawResources = Array.isArray(value) ? value : fallback
         414	    return rawResources
         415	      .map((resource) => this.record(resource))
         416	      .map((resource) => ({
         417	        file_path: this.stringValue(resource.file_path) ?? '',
         418	        content_type: this.stringValue(resource.content_type) ?? 'text/markdown',
         419	        content: this.stringValue(resource.content) ?? '',
         420	        storage_url: this.stringValue(resource.storage_url),
         421	      }))
         422	      .filter((resource) => resource.file_path.length > 0)
         423	  }
         424
         425	  private statusForDecision(decision: AgentLearningExperimentDecision): SkillRecommendationRow['status'] {
         426	    if (decision === 'keep') return 'kept'
         427	    if (decision === 'revise') return 'revising'
         428	    if (decision === 'revert') return 'reverted'
         429	    return 'inconclusive'
         430	  }
         431
         432	  private elapsedDays(startedAt: string): number {
         433	    const start = new Date(startedAt).getTime()
         434	    if (!Number.isFinite(start)) return 0
         435	    return Math.max(0, Math.floor((Date.now() - start) / (24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)))
         436	  }
         437
         438	  private record(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> {
         439	    if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return {}
         440	    return value as Record<string, unknown>
         441	  }
         442
         443	  private stringValue(value: unknown): string | null {
         444	    return typeof value === 'string' && value.trim().length > 0 ? value : null
         445	  }
         446
         447	  private numberValue(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
         448	    return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : fallback
         449	  }
         450	}

         137	@Injectable()
         138	export class AgentLearningLoopPolicyService {
         139	  classifyCandidate(input: AgentLearningCandidateInput): AgentLearningClassification {
         140	    const platformOwned =
         141	      input.ownership === 'platform' ||
         142	      input.artifactKind === 'tool_schema' ||
         143	      input.evidenceKinds.includes('tool_contract_problem')
         144
         145	    if (platformOwned) {
         146	      return this.routeOut(input, 'product_fix_proposal')
         147	    }
         148
         149	    if (input.ownership === 'system') {
         150	      return this.routeOut(input, 'system_artifact_internal_review')
         151	    }
         152
         153	    const agentFileKey = this.resolveAgentFileTarget(input.evidenceKinds)
         154	    if (agentFileKey) {
         155	      return this.customerProposal(input, 'agent_file_update', 'agent_file', agentFileKey)
         156	    }
         157
         158	    if (
         159	      input.artifactKind === 'skill_resource' ||
         160	      input.evidenceKinds.includes('missing_skill_reference')
         161	    ) {
         162	      const skillKey = input.artifactKey ?? input.suggestedSkillKey ?? 'skill-reference'
         163	      return this.customerProposal(input, 'skill_resource_update', 'skill_resource', skillKey)
         164	    }
         165
         166	    if (input.artifactKind === 'skill') {
         167	      const skillKey = input.artifactKey ?? input.suggestedSkillKey ?? 'new-skill'
         168	      const proposalKind = input.artifactKey ? 'skill_update' : 'skill_create'
         169	      return this.customerProposal(input, proposalKind, 'skill', skillKey)
         170	    }
         171
         172	    return this.routeOut(input, 'unsupported_scope')
         173	  }
         174
         175	  scoreCandidate(input: AgentLearningScoreInput): AgentLearningScoreResult {
         176	    const scopeFit = this.clamp(input.scopeFit)
         177	    if (scopeFit <= 0) {
         178	      return {
         179	        score: 0,
         180	        band: 'blocked',
         181	        eligibleForProposal: false,
         182	        blockedReason: 'scope_fit_failed',
         183	      }
         184	    }
         185
         186	    const weightedScore =
         187	      0.35 * this.clamp(input.userValue) +
         188	      0.25 * this.clamp(input.recurrence) +
         189	      0.2 * this.clamp(input.evidenceConfidence) +
         190	      0.1 * this.clamp(input.blastRadius) +
         191	      0.1 * this.clamp(input.freshness)
         192	    const score = Math.round(weightedScore * scopeFit * 100)
         193	    const band = this.scoreBand(score)
         194
         195	    return {
         196	      score,
         197	      band,
         198	      eligibleForProposal: score >= 55,
         199	      blockedReason: null,
         200	    }
         201	  }
         202
         203	  evaluateExperiment(input: AgentLearningExperimentInput): AgentLearningExperimentResult {
         204	    const minimumEvents = input.minimumQualifyingEvents ?? 5
         205	    const enoughEvents = input.enoughEvents ?? 20
         206	    const enoughDays = input.enoughDays ?? 14
         207	    const primaryChangePct = this.percentChange(
         208	      input.baseline.primarySuccessRate,
         209	      input.current.primarySuccessRate,
         210	    )
         211	    const toolErrorWorseningPct = this.worseningPercent(
         212	      input.baseline.toolErrorRate,
         213	      input.current.toolErrorRate,
         214	    )
         215	    const roleViolationWorseningPct = this.worseningPercent(
         216	      input.baseline.roleViolationRate,
         217	      input.current.roleViolationRate,
         218	    )
         219	    const negativeFeedbackWorseningPct = this.worseningPercent(
         220	      input.baseline.negativeFeedbackRate,
         221	      input.current.negativeFeedbackRate,
         222	    )
         223	    const maxGuardrailWorseningPct = Math.max(
         224	      toolErrorWorseningPct,
         225	      roleViolationWorseningPct,
         226	      negativeFeedbackWorseningPct,
         227	    )
         228
         229	    if (input.qualifyingEvents < minimumEvents) {
         230	      return {
         231	        decision: 'inconclusive',
         232	        primaryChangePct,
         233	        maxGuardrailWorseningPct,
         234	        reasons: ['not_enough_minimum_events'],
         235	      }
         236	    }
         237
         238	    if (input.qualifyingEvents < enoughEvents && input.elapsedDays < enoughDays) {
         239	      return {
         240	        decision: 'inconclusive',
         241	        primaryChangePct,
         242	        maxGuardrailWorseningPct,
         243	        reasons: ['evidence_window_open'],
         244	      }
         245	    }
         246
         247	    if (
         248	      primaryChangePct < 0 ||
         249	      maxGuardrailWorseningPct > 20 ||
         250	      roleViolationWorseningPct > 0 ||
         251	      (input.trustedNegativeFeedbackCount ?? 0) > 0
         252	    ) {
         253	      return {
         254	        decision: 'revert',
         255	        primaryChangePct,
         256	        maxGuardrailWorseningPct,
         257	        reasons: ['regression_detected'],
         258	      }
         259	    }
         260
         261	    if (primaryChangePct >= 30 && maxGuardrailWorseningPct <= 10) {
         262	      return {
         263	        decision: 'keep',
         264	        primaryChangePct,
         265	        maxGuardrailWorseningPct,
         266	        reasons: ['strong_primary_improvement'],
         267	      }
         268	    }
         269
         270	    if (primaryChangePct >= 10 || maxGuardrailWorseningPct >= 10) {
         271	      return {
         272	        decision: 'revise',
         273	        primaryChangePct,
         274	        maxGuardrailWorseningPct,
         275	        reasons: ['partial_or_noisy_improvement'],
         276	      }
         277	    }
         278
         279	    return {
         280	      decision: 'inconclusive',
         281	      primaryChangePct,
         282	      maxGuardrailWorseningPct,
         283	      reasons: ['low_signal_change'],
         284	    }
         285	  }
         286
         287	  resolveProposalConflict(input: AgentLearningConflictInput): AgentLearningConflictResult {
         288	    const runningExperiment = input.runningExperiments.find(
         289	      (experiment) =>
         290	        experiment.artifactLockKey === input.artifactLockKey && experiment.status === 'running',
         291	    )
         292	    if (runningExperiment) {
         293	      return {
         294	        action: 'wait_for_running_experiment',
         295	        proposalId: null,
         296	        experimentId: runningExperiment.id,
         297	      }
         298	    }
         299
         300	    const pendingProposal = input.pendingProposals.find(
         301	      (proposal) =>
         302	        proposal.artifactLockKey === input.artifactLockKey && proposal.status === 'pending',
         303	    )
         304	    if (pendingProposal) {
         305	      return {
         306	        action: 'patch_existing_pending_proposal',
         307	        proposalId: pendingProposal.id,
         308	        experimentId: null,
         309	      }
         310	    }
         311
         312	    return {
         313	      action: 'create_new_proposal',
         314	      proposalId: null,
         315	      experimentId: null,
         316	    }
         317	  }
         318
         319	  evaluateProposalQuality(
         320	    input: AgentLearningProposalQualityInput,
         321	  ): AgentLearningProposalQualityResult {
         322	    const failures: string[] = []
         323
         324	    if (input.evidenceEventIds.length < 3) failures.push('minimum_evidence_required')
         325	    if (!input.hasWhy) failures.push('why_required')
         326	    if (!input.hasTrigger) failures.push('trigger_required')
         327	    if (!input.hasDecisionRules) failures.push('decision_rules_required')
         328	    if (!input.hasConcreteExamples) failures.push('concrete_examples_required')
         329	    if (!input.hasExpectedOutput) failures.push('expected_output_required')
         330	    if (input.privateDataRisk !== 'none') failures.push('private_data_risk')
         331
         332	    return {
         333	      ok: failures.length === 0,
         334	      failures,
         335	    }
         336	  }
         337
         338	  private customerProposal(
         339	    input: AgentLearningCandidateInput,
         340	    proposalKind: Exclude<AgentLearningProposalKind, 'route_out'>,
         341	    artifactKind: AgentLearningArtifactKind,
         342	    artifactKey: string,
         343	  ): AgentLearningClassification {
         344	    return {
         345	      proposalKind,
         346	      routeOutType: null,
         347	      customerVisible: true,
         348	      targetAgentKey: input.targetAgentKey,
         349	      targetArtifactKind: artifactKind,
         350	      targetArtifactKey: artifactKey,
         351	      artifactLockKey: this.artifactLockKey(input.orgId, input.targetAgentKey, artifactKind, artifactKey),
         352	      reason: 'Jaime can propose this org-owned agent or skill change.',
         353	    }
         354	  }
         355
         356	  private routeOut(
         357	    input: AgentLearningCandidateInput,
         358	    routeOutType: AgentLearningRouteOutType,
         359	  ): AgentLearningClassification {
         360	    const artifactKey = input.artifactKey ?? input.suggestedSkillKey ?? 'unknown'
         361	    return {
         362	      proposalKind: 'route_out',
         363	      routeOutType,
         364	      customerVisible: false,
         365	      targetAgentKey: input.targetAgentKey,
         366	      targetArtifactKind: input.artifactKind,
         367	      targetArtifactKey: artifactKey,
         368	      artifactLockKey: this.artifactLockKey(
         369	        input.ownership === 'org' ? input.orgId : input.ownership,
         370	        input.targetAgentKey,
         371	        input.artifactKind,
         372	        artifactKey,
         373	      ),
         374	      reason:
         375	        routeOutType === 'product_fix_proposal'
         376	          ? 'Platform-owned tool or schema issues require an internal product fix proposal.'
         377	          : 'System-owned artifacts require internal Vibey review, not a customer-visible recommendation.',
         378	    }
         379	  }
         380
         381	  private artifactLockKey(
         382	    scopeKey: string,
         383	    targetAgentKey: string,
         384	    artifactKind: AgentLearningArtifactKind,
         385	    artifactKey: string,
         386	  ): string {
         387	    return [scopeKey, targetAgentKey, artifactKind, artifactKey].join(':')
         388	  }
         389
         390	  private resolveAgentFileTarget(
         391	    evidenceKinds: AgentLearningEvidenceKind[],
         392	  ): 'ROLE.md' | 'IDENTITY.md' | 'SOUL.md' | null {
         393	    if (evidenceKinds.includes('role_boundary_violation')) return 'ROLE.md'
         394	    if (evidenceKinds.includes('identity_confusion')) return 'IDENTITY.md'
         395	    if (evidenceKinds.includes('tone_or_values_mismatch')) return 'SOUL.md'
         396	    return null
         397	  }
         398
         399	  private scoreBand(score: number): AgentLearningScoreBand {
         400	    if (score >= 75) return 'high'
         401	    if (score >= 55) return 'medium'
         402	    return 'low'
         403	  }
         404
         405	  private percentChange(baseline: number, current: number): number {
         406	    if (baseline === 0) return current > 0 ? 100 : 0
         407	    return Math.round(((current - baseline) / baseline) * 100)
         408	  }
         409
         410	  private worseningPercent(baseline: number, current: number): number {
         411	    return Math.max(0, this.percentChange(baseline, current))
         412	  }
         413
         414	  private clamp(value: number): number {
         415	    if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return 0
         416	    return Math.min(Math.max(value, 0), 1)
         417	  }
         418	}
           1	import { Injectable, Logger } from '@nestjs/common'
           2	import { SkillRecommendationsRepository } from '../repositories/skill-recommendations.repository'
           3	import type { SkillRecommendationEventRow } from '../types/skill-recommendations.types'
           4	import { SkillRecommendationJobsService } from './skill-recommendation-jobs.service'
           5
           6	type EventGroup = {
           7	  key: string
           8	  agentKey: string
           9	  promptFingerprint: string
          10	  toolSignature: string
          11	  events: SkillRecommendationEventRow[]
          12	}
          13
          14	@Injectable()
          15	export class SkillRecommendationDetectionService {
          16	  private readonly logger = new Logger(SkillRecommendationDetectionService.name)
          17
          18	  constructor(
          19	    private readonly repository: SkillRecommendationsRepository,
          20	    private readonly jobs: SkillRecommendationJobsService,
          21	  ) {}
          22
          23	  async scanOrg(orgId: string): Promise<{ candidates: number; jobs: number }> {
          24	    const since = new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString()
          25	    const [{ data, error }, systemAgentKeys] = await Promise.all([
          26	      this.repository.listRecentEvents(orgId, since),
          27	      this.loadSystemAgentKeys(),
          28	    ])
          29
          30	    if (error) throw new Error(`Failed to scan skill recommendation events: ${error.message}`)
          31
          32	    const groups = this.groupEvents((data ?? []) as SkillRecommendationEventRow[], systemAgentKeys)
          33	    let candidates = 0
          34	    let jobs = 0
          35	    for (const group of groups) {
          36	      if (group.events.length < 3) continue
          37	      const candidateId = await this.upsertCandidate(orgId, group)
          38	      candidates += 1
          39	      const latestEvent = group.events[0]
          40	      if (latestEvent) {
          41	        const queued = await this.jobs.enqueueCandidateReview({
          42	          userId: latestEvent.user_id,
          43	          orgId,
          44	          candidateId,
          45	          triggerEventId: latestEvent.id,
          46	        })
          47	        if (!queued.deduped) jobs += 1
          48	      }
          49	    }
          50	    return { candidates, jobs }
          51	  }
          52
          53	  private groupEvents(
          54	    rows: SkillRecommendationEventRow[],
          55	    systemAgentKeys: Set<string>,
          56	  ): EventGroup[] {
          57	    const groups = new Map<string, EventGroup>()
          58	    for (const row of rows) {
          59	      if (systemAgentKeys.has(row.agent_key.toLowerCase())) continue
          60	      if ((row.skill_keys_used ?? []).length > 0) continue
          61	      if ((row.workflow_keys_used ?? []).length > 0) continue
          62	      const key = [row.agent_key, row.prompt_fingerprint, row.tool_signature || ''].join('::')
          63	      const group =
          64	        groups.get(key) ??
          65	        ({
          66	          key,
          67	          agentKey: row.agent_key,
          68	          promptFingerprint: row.prompt_fingerprint,
          69	          toolSignature: row.tool_signature || '',
          70	          events: [],
          71	        } satisfies EventGroup)
          72	      group.events.push(row)
          73	      groups.set(key, group)
          74	    }
          75	    return [...groups.values()]
          76	  }
          77
          78	  private async loadSystemAgentKeys(): Promise<Set<string>> {
          79	    const { data, error } = await this.repository.listSystemAgentKeys()
          80	    if (error) throw new Error(`Failed to load system agent keys: ${error.message}`)
          81	    return new Set(
          82	      ((data ?? []) as Array<{ agent_key?: unknown }>)
          83	        .map((row) => (typeof row.agent_key === 'string' ? row.agent_key.toLowerCase() : null))
          84	        .filter((agentKey): agentKey is string => Boolean(agentKey)),
          85	    )
          86	  }
          87
          88	  private async upsertCandidate(orgId: string, group: EventGroup): Promise<string> {
          89	    const sorted = [...group.events].sort(
          90	      (a, b) => new Date(b.created_at).getTime() - new Date(a.created_at).getTime(),
          91	    )
          92	    const newest = sorted[0]
          93	    const oldest = sorted[sorted.length - 1]
          94	    const toolNames = [...new Set(sorted.flatMap((event) => event.tool_names ?? []))]
          95	    const evidenceIds = sorted.map((event) => event.id)
          96
          97	    const { data, error } = await this.repository.upsertCandidate({
          98	      org_id: orgId,
          99	      agent_key: group.agentKey,
         100	      prompt_fingerprint: group.promptFingerprint,
         101	      tool_signature: group.toolSignature,
         102	      tool_names: toolNames,
         103	      run_count: sorted.length,
         104	      evidence_event_ids: evidenceIds,
         105	      first_event_at: oldest?.created_at ?? null,
         106	      last_event_at: newest?.created_at ?? null,
         107	    })
         108
         109	    if (error || !data?.id) {
         110	      this.logger.warn(`Candidate upsert failed for ${group.key}: ${error?.message}`)
         111	      throw new Error(`Failed to upsert skill recommendation candidate: ${error?.message}`)
         112	    }
         113
         114	    return data.id as string
         115	  }
         116	}
           1	import { Injectable, Logger, OnModuleDestroy, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common'

          15	@Injectable()
          16	export class SkillRecommendationJobsService implements OnModuleInit, OnModuleDestroy {
          17	  private readonly logger = new Logger(SkillRecommendationJobsService.name)
          18	  private readonly pollIntervalMs = 10_000
          19	  private readonly maxAttempts = 3
          20	  private readonly maxTraceEvidence = 3
          21	  private readonly maxTraceTextChars = 6000
          22	  private readonly maxTraceJsonChars = 12000
          23	  private timer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null
          24	  private processing = false
          25	  private activeJobCount = 0
          26
          27	  constructor(
          28	    private readonly repository: SkillRecommendationsRepository,
          29	    private readonly learningRepository: AgentLearningLoopRepository,
          30	    private readonly jaime: SkillRecommendationJaimeService,
          31	    private readonly errorReporter: ErrorReporter,
          32	  ) {}
          33
          34	  onModuleInit() {
          35	    if (process.env.DISABLE_SKILL_RECOMMENDATION_POLLER === '1') return
          36	    this.timer = setInterval(() => void this.processDueJobs(), this.pollIntervalMs)
          37	    void this.processDueJobs()
          38	  }
          39
          40	  onModuleDestroy() {
          41	    if (this.timer) {
          42	      clearInterval(this.timer)
          43	      this.timer = null
          44	    }
          45	  }
