          47	  async enqueueCandidateReview(input: {
          48	    userId: string
          49	    orgId: string
          50	    candidateId: string
          51	    triggerEventId?: string
          52	  }): Promise<{ jobId: string; status: SkillRecommendationJobStatus; deduped: boolean }> {
          53	    const dedupeKey = `agent-improvement:${input.candidateId}`
          54	    const { data: existing, error: existingError } = await this.repository.findActiveJob(
          55	      input.orgId,
          56	      dedupeKey,
          57	    )
          58
          59	    if (existingError) throw new Error(`DB error: ${existingError.message}`)
          60	    if (existing?.id) {
          61	      return {
          62	        jobId: existing.id as string,
          63	        status: existing.status as SkillRecommendationJobStatus,
          64	        deduped: true,
          65	      }
          66	    }
          67
          68	    const { data, error } = await this.repository.insertJob({
          69	      user_id: input.userId,
          70	      org_id: input.orgId,
          71	      candidate_id: input.candidateId,
          72	      dedupe_key: dedupeKey,
          73	      payload: {
          74	        candidate_id: input.candidateId,
          75	        trigger_event_id: input.triggerEventId ?? null,
          76	      },
          77	      status: 'queued',
          78	      attempts: 0,
          79	      max_attempts: this.maxAttempts,
          80	      next_attempt_at: new Date().toISOString(),
          81	    })
          82
          83	    if (
          84	      error?.message?.includes('uq_agent_improvement_jobs_active_dedupe') ||
          85	      error?.message?.includes('uq_skill_recommendation_jobs_active_dedupe')
          86	    ) {
          87	      const { data: raced } = await this.repository.findActiveJob(input.orgId, dedupeKey)
          88	      if (raced?.id) {
          89	        return {
          90	          jobId: raced.id as string,
          91	          status: raced.status as SkillRecommendationJobStatus,
          92	          deduped: true,
          93	        }
          94	      }
          95	    }
          96
          97	    if (error || !data) throw new Error(`DB error: ${error?.message ?? 'Failed to enqueue job'}`)
          98
          99	    await this.repository.markOpenCandidateQueued(input.candidateId)
         100
         101	    void this.processDueJobs()
         102	    return {
         103	      jobId: data.id as string,
         104	      status: data.status as SkillRecommendationJobStatus,
         105	      deduped: false,
         106	    }
         107	  }
         108
         109	  async processDueJobs(): Promise<void> {
         110	    if (this.processing) return
         111	    this.processing = true
         112	    let jobs: SkillRecommendationJobRow[] = []
         113	    try {
         114	      await this.recoverStaleJobs()
         115	      const slots = 2 - this.activeJobCount
         116	      if (slots <= 0) return
         117	      const { data, error } = await this.repository.listDueJobs(slots, new Date().toISOString())
         118	      if (error) throw new Error(`DB error: ${error.message}`)
         119	      for (const raw of data ?? []) {
         120	        const claimed = await this.claimJob(raw as SkillRecommendationJobRow)
         121	        if (claimed) jobs.push(claimed)
         122	      }
         123	      this.activeJobCount += jobs.length
         124	    } catch (error) {
         125	      const message = (error as Error).message
         126	      this.logger.warn(`Skill recommendation queue cycle failed: ${message}`)
         127	      reportAppError(this.errorReporter, {
         128	        app: process.env.APP_NAME ?? 'api',
         129	        category: 'worker',
         130	        feature: 'agent_improvement_proposals/jobs',
         131	        error_code: 'queue_cycle_failed',
         132	        message,
         133	      })
         134	    } finally {
         135	      this.processing = false
         136	    }
         137
         138	    for (const job of jobs) {
         139	      void this.executeClaimedJob(job)
         140	        .catch((error) => {
         141	          const message = (error as Error).message
         142	          this.logger.error(`Skill recommendation job ${job.id} failed: ${message}`)
         143	          reportAppError(this.errorReporter, {
         144	            app: process.env.APP_NAME ?? 'api',
         145	            category: 'worker',
         146	            feature: 'agent_improvement_proposals/jobs',
         147	            error_code: 'job_failed',
         148	            message,
         149	            user_id: job.user_id,
         150	            context: { jobId: job.id, candidateId: job.candidate_id },
         151	          })
         152	        })
         153	        .finally(() => {
         154	          this.activeJobCount -= 1
         155	        })
         156	    }
         157	  }
         158
         159	  private async recoverStaleJobs(): Promise<void> {
         160	    const staleThreshold = new Date(Date.now() - 10 * 60 * 1000).toISOString()
         161	    const { data } = await this.repository.listStaleProcessingJobs(staleThreshold)
         162	    for (const row of data ?? []) {
         163	      const attempts = Number(row.attempts ?? 0)
         164	      const maxAttempts = Number(row.max_attempts ?? this.maxAttempts)
         165	      const nextStatus = attempts >= maxAttempts ? 'failed' : 'retry'
         166	      await this.repository.updateStaleJob(row.id, {
         167	        status: nextStatus,
         168	        last_error: 'Recovered: stuck in processing beyond 10 minutes',
         169	        completed_at: nextStatus === 'failed' ? new Date().toISOString() : null,
         170	        next_attempt_at: new Date().toISOString(),
         171	      })
         172	    }
         173	  }
         174
         175	  private async claimJob(
         176	    job: SkillRecommendationJobRow,
         177	  ): Promise<SkillRecommendationJobRow | null> {
         178	    const attempts = Number(job.attempts || 0) + 1
         179	    const { data, error } = await this.repository.claimJob(job, attempts)
         180	    if (error) throw new Error(`DB error: ${error.message}`)
         181	    return (data as SkillRecommendationJobRow | null) ?? null
         182	  }
         183
         184	  private async executeClaimedJob(job: SkillRecommendationJobRow): Promise<void> {
         185	    try {
         186	      await this.repository.markCandidateProcessing(job.candidate_id)
         187
         188	      const candidate = await this.loadCandidate(job.candidate_id)
         189	      const events = await this.loadEvents(candidate)
         190	      const traceEvidence = await this.loadTraceEvidence(job.org_id, events)
         191	      const existingSkills = await this.loadExistingSkills(job.org_id, candidate.agent_key)
         192	      const feedbackSummary = await this.loadFeedbackSummary(job.org_id, candidate)
         193	      const review = await this.jaime.reviewCandidate({
         194	        job,
         195	        candidate,
         196	        events,
         197	        traceEvidence,
         198	        existingSkills,
         199	        feedbackSummary,
         200	      })
         201
         202	      if (review.verdict === 'skip') {
         203	        await this.repository.updateCandidate(candidate.id, {
         204	          status: 'skipped',
         205	          skip_reason: review.reason,
         206	        })
         207	        await this.markSucceeded(job, { verdict: 'skip', reason: review.reason, raw: review.raw })
         208	        return
         209	      }
         210
         211	      const payload = this.buildRecommendationPayload(job, candidate, review.proposal)
         212	      if (payload.proposal_kind === 'route_out') {
         213	        const { data: routeOut, error: routeOutError } =
         214	          await this.repository.upsertRecommendation(payload)
         215	        if (routeOutError || !routeOut?.id) {
         216	          throw new Error(`Failed to save Jaime route-out: ${routeOutError?.message}`)
         217	        }
         218	        await this.repository.updateCandidate(candidate.id, { status: 'routed_out' })
         219	        await this.markSucceeded(job, {
         220	          verdict: 'route_out',
         221	          recommendation_id: routeOut.id,
         222	          raw: review.raw,
         223	        })
         224	        return
         225	      }
         226
         227	      const artifactLockKey = String(payload.artifact_lock_key ?? '')
         228	      if (artifactLockKey) {
         229	        const { data: runningExperiment, error: experimentError } =
         230	          await this.learningRepository.findRunningExperimentByArtifactLockKey(
         231	            job.org_id,
         232	            artifactLockKey,
         233	          )
         234	        if (experimentError) {
         235	          throw new Error(`Failed to check running experiment: ${experimentError.message}`)
         236	        }
         237	        if (runningExperiment?.id) {
         238	          await this.repository.updateCandidate(candidate.id, {
         239	            status: 'skipped',
         240	            skip_reason: 'artifact_has_running_experiment',
         241	          })
         242	          await this.markSucceeded(job, {
         243	            verdict: 'wait_for_running_experiment',
         244	            experiment_id: runningExperiment.id,
         245	            raw: review.raw,
         246	          })
         247	          return
         248	        }
         249
         250	        const { data: existingProposal, error: existingError } =
         251	          await this.learningRepository.findReadyRecommendationByArtifactLockKey(
         252	            job.org_id,
         253	            artifactLockKey,
         254	          )
         255	        if (existingError) {
         256	          throw new Error(`Failed to check existing proposal: ${existingError.message}`)
         257	        }
         258	        if (existingProposal?.id) {
         259	          const { data: patched, error: patchError } =
         260	            await this.learningRepository.updateRecommendationProposal(
         261	              job.org_id,
         262	              existingProposal.id,
         263	              payload,
         264	            )
         265	          if (patchError || !patched?.id) {
         266	            throw new Error(`Failed to patch Jaime proposal: ${patchError?.message}`)
         267	          }
         268	          await this.repository.updateCandidate(candidate.id, { status: 'recommended' })
         269	          await this.markSucceeded(job, {
         270	            verdict: 'patched_existing_proposal',
         271	            recommendation_id: patched.id,
         272	            raw: review.raw,
         273	          })
         274	          return
         275	        }
         276	      }
         277
         278	      const { data: recommendation, error: insertError } =
         279	        await this.repository.upsertRecommendation(payload)
         280
         281	      if (insertError || !recommendation?.id) {
         282	        throw new Error(`Failed to save Jaime proposal: ${insertError?.message}`)
         283	      }
         284
         285	      await this.repository.updateCandidate(candidate.id, { status: 'recommended' })
         286	      await this.markSucceeded(job, {
         287	        verdict: 'recommend',
         288	        recommendation_id: recommendation.id,
         289	        raw: review.raw,
         290	      })
         291	    } catch (error) {
         292	      await this.markFailedOrRetry(job, error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error')
         293	    }
         294	  }

         296	  private async loadCandidate(candidateId: string): Promise<SkillRecommendationCandidateRow> {
         297	    const { data, error } = await this.repository.loadCandidate(candidateId)
         298	    if (error || !data) throw new Error(`Candidate not found: ${error?.message ?? candidateId}`)
         299	    return data as SkillRecommendationCandidateRow
         300	  }

         302	  private async loadEvents(
         303	    candidate: SkillRecommendationCandidateRow,
         304	  ): Promise<SkillRecommendationEventRow[]> {
         305	    const eventIds = candidate.evidence_event_ids.slice(0, 8)
         306	    if (eventIds.length === 0) return []
         307	    const { data, error } = await this.repository.loadEvents(eventIds)
         308	    if (error) throw new Error(`Failed to load recommendation events: ${error.message}`)
         309	    return (data ?? []) as SkillRecommendationEventRow[]
         310	  }
         311
         312	  private async loadTraceEvidence(
         313	    orgId: string,
         314	    events: SkillRecommendationEventRow[],
         315	  ): Promise<SkillRecommendationTraceEvidence[]> {
         316	    const traceIds = [
         317	      ...new Set(
         318	        events
         319	          .map((event) => event.trace_id)
         320	          .filter(
         321	            (traceId): traceId is string => typeof traceId === 'string' && traceId.length > 0,
         322	          ),
         323	      ),
         324	    ].slice(0, this.maxTraceEvidence)
         325	    if (traceIds.length === 0) return []
         326
         327	    const { data, error } = await this.repository.loadTraceRows(orgId, traceIds)
         328
         329	    if (error) {
         330	      this.logger.warn(`Failed to hydrate skill recommendation traces: ${error.message}`)
         331	      return []
         332	    }
         333
         334	    const byTraceId = new Map<string, Record<string, unknown>>()
         335	    for (const row of data ?? []) {
         336	      if (typeof row.id === 'string') byTraceId.set(row.id, row as Record<string, unknown>)
         337	    }
         338
         339	    return events
         340	      .filter((event) => event.trace_id && byTraceId.has(event.trace_id))
         341	      .slice(0, this.maxTraceEvidence)
         342	      .map((event) => {
         343	        const trace = byTraceId.get(event.trace_id!)!
         344	        return {
         345	          event_id: event.id,
         346	          trace_id: event.trace_id!,
         347	          user_message: this.compactTraceText(trace.user_message, this.maxTraceTextChars),
         348	          agent_response: this.compactTraceText(trace.response, this.maxTraceTextChars),
         349	          tool_steps_excerpt: this.compactTraceJson(trace.tool_steps, this.maxTraceJsonChars),
         350	          messages_input_excerpt: this.compactTraceJson(
         351	            trace.messages_input,
         352	            this.maxTraceJsonChars,
         353	          ),
         354	          messages_output_excerpt: this.compactTraceJson(
         355	            trace.messages_output,
         356	            this.maxTraceJsonChars,
         357	          ),
         358	          system_prompt_excerpt: this.compactTraceText(trace.system_prompt, this.maxTraceTextChars),
         359	          model: typeof trace.model === 'string' ? trace.model : null,
         360	          status: typeof trace.status === 'string' ? trace.status : null,
         361	          total_tokens: typeof trace.total_tokens === 'number' ? trace.total_tokens : null,
         362	          duration_ms: typeof trace.duration_ms === 'number' ? trace.duration_ms : null,
         363	          completed_at: typeof trace.completed_at === 'string' ? trace.completed_at : null,
         364	        }
         365	      })
         366	  }
         367
         368	  private async loadExistingSkills(
         369	    orgId: string,
         370	    agentKey: string,
         371	  ): Promise<Array<{ skill_key: string; name: string; description: string }>> {
         372	    const { data, error } = await this.repository.listExistingSkills(orgId, agentKey)

         432	  private async markFailedOrRetry(job: SkillRecommendationJobRow, message: string): Promise<void> {
         433	    const nextStatus = job.attempts >= (job.max_attempts || this.maxAttempts) ? 'failed' : 'retry'
         434	    const nextAttemptAt = new Date(Date.now() + this.getBackoffMs(job.attempts)).toISOString()
         435	    const { error } = await this.repository.markJobFailedOrRetry(
         436	      job,
         437	      nextStatus,
         438	      message,
         439	      nextAttemptAt,
         440	    )
         441	    if (error) {
         442	      this.logger.warn(`Failed to update job failure state: ${error.message}`)
         443	      reportAppError(this.errorReporter, {

         445	        category: 'worker',

         447	        error_code: 'failure_state_update_failed',
         448	        message: error.message,
         449	        user_id: job.user_id,
         450	        context: { jobId: job.id },
         451	      })
         452	    }
         453	  }

         460	  private compactTraceJson(value: unknown, maxChars: number): string | null {
         461	    if (value === null || value === undefined) return null
         462	    try {
         463	      return this.compactTraceText(JSON.stringify(value), maxChars)
         464	    } catch {
         465	      return this.compactTraceText(String(value), maxChars)
         466	    }
         467	  }
         468
         469	  private compactTraceText(value: unknown, maxChars: number): string | null {
         470	    if (typeof value !== 'string') return null
         471	    const cleaned = value
         472	      .replace(/https?:\/\/\S+/g, '[url]')
         473	      .replace(/[a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}/gi, '[email]')
         474	      .replace(/[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f-]{27,}/gi, '[id]')
         475	      .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
         476	      .trim()
         477	    if (!cleaned) return null
         478	    if (cleaned.length <= maxChars) return cleaned
         479	    return `${cleaned.slice(0, maxChars)}...[truncated]`
         480	  }

           1	-- Ad analytics RPC for campaign dashboard
           2	create or replace function public.get_campaign_ad_analytics(
           3	  p_campaign_id uuid,
           4	  p_start_date timestamp with time zone default null,
           5	  p_end_date timestamp with time zone default null
           6	) returns json
           7	language plpgsql
           8	security definer
           9	set search_path to 'public'
          10	as $function$
          11	declare
          12	  result json;
          13	begin
          14	  with ad_visitors as (
          15	    select
          16	      count(distinct visitor_hash) as unique_visitors,
          17	      count(*) as total_views
          18	    from public.visitors_page_views
          19	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
          20	      and utm_content is not null
          21	      and (p_start_date is null or viewed_at >= p_start_date)
          22	      and (p_end_date is null or viewed_at <= p_end_date)
          23	  ),
          24	  ad_leads as (
          25	    select count(*) as total_leads
          26	    from public.leads
          27	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
          28	      and ad_id is not null
          29	      and (p_start_date is null or created_at >= p_start_date)
          30	      and (p_end_date is null or created_at <= p_end_date)
          31	  ),
          32	  active_ads as (
          33	    select count(*) as total_ads
          34	    from public.ads
          35	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
          36	  ),
          37	  daily_leads as (
          38	    select date(created_at) as day, count(*) as leads
          39	    from public.leads
          40	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
          41	      and ad_id is not null
          42	      and (p_start_date is null or created_at >= p_start_date)
          43	      and (p_end_date is null or created_at <= p_end_date)
          44	    group by date(created_at)
          45	  ),
          46	  daily_visitors as (
          47	    select date(viewed_at) as day, count(distinct visitor_hash) as visitors
          48	    from public.visitors_page_views
          49	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
          50	      and utm_content is not null
          51	      and (p_start_date is null or viewed_at >= p_start_date)
          52	      and (p_end_date is null or viewed_at <= p_end_date)
          53	    group by date(viewed_at)
          54	  ),
          55	  daily as (
          56	    select
          57	      coalesce(dv.day, dl.day) as day,
          58	      coalesce(dv.visitors, 0) as visitors,
          59	      coalesce(dl.leads, 0) as leads
          60	    from daily_visitors dv
          61	    full outer join daily_leads dl on dl.day = dv.day
          62	    order by day
          63	  ),
          64	  campaign_breakdown as (
          65	    select
          66	      ac.id as ad_campaign_id,
          67	      ac.name as campaign_name,
          68	      ac.objective,
          69	      (select count(*) from public.ad_sets s where s.ad_campaign_id = ac.id) as ad_sets_count,
          70	      (select count(*) from public.ads a2 join public.ad_sets s2 on s2.id = a2.ad_set_id where s2.ad_campaign_id = ac.id) as ads_count,
          71	      (select count(*) from public.leads l2 where l2.ad_campaign_id = ac.id
          72	        and (p_start_date is null or l2.created_at >= p_start_date)
          73	        and (p_end_date is null or l2.created_at <= p_end_date)
          74	      ) as leads_count,
          75	      (select coalesce(sum(s3.daily_budget), 0) from public.ad_sets s3 where s3.ad_campaign_id = ac.id) as total_daily_budget
          76	    from public.ad_campaigns ac
          77	    where ac.campaign_id = p_campaign_id
          78	  )
          79	  select json_build_object(
          80	    'ad_visitors', coalesce((select unique_visitors from ad_visitors), 0),
          81	    'ad_views', coalesce((select total_views from ad_visitors), 0),
          82	    'ad_leads', coalesce((select total_leads from ad_leads), 0),
          83	    'total_ads', coalesce((select total_ads from active_ads), 0),
          84	    'conversion_rate', case
          85	      when coalesce((select unique_visitors from ad_visitors), 0) = 0 then 0
          86	      else round(coalesce((select total_leads from ad_leads), 0)::numeric / (select unique_visitors from ad_visitors) * 100, 2)
          87	    end,
          88	    'chart_data', coalesce((select json_agg(json_build_object('date', day, 'visitors', visitors, 'leads', leads)) from daily), '[]'::json),
          89	    'breakdown', coalesce((select json_agg(json_build_object(
          90	      'ad_campaign_id', ad_campaign_id,
          91	      'campaign_name', campaign_name,
          92	      'objective', objective,
          93	      'ad_sets_count', ad_sets_count,
          94	      'ads_count', ads_count,
          95	      'leads_count', leads_count,
          96	      'daily_budget', total_daily_budget
          97	    )) from campaign_breakdown), '[]'::json)
          98	  ) into result;
          99
         100	  return result;
         101	end;
         102	$function$;

         144	create or replace function public.get_campaign_analytics(
         145	  p_campaign_id uuid,

         157	    select
         158	      count(*) as total_views,
         159	      count(distinct visitor_hash) as unique_visitors
         160	    from public.visitors_page_views
         161	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
         162	      and (p_start_date is null or viewed_at >= p_start_date)
         163	      and (p_end_date is null or viewed_at <= p_end_date)
         164	  ),

         167	      count(*) as total_leads
         168	    from public.leads
         169	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
         170	      and (p_start_date is null or created_at >= p_start_date)
         171	      and (p_end_date is null or created_at <= p_end_date)
         172	  ),
         173	  daily_views as (
         174	    select
         175	      date(viewed_at) as day,
         176	      count(distinct visitor_hash) as visitors
         177	    from public.visitors_page_views
         178	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
         179	      and (p_start_date is null or viewed_at >= p_start_date)
         180	      and (p_end_date is null or viewed_at <= p_end_date)
         181	    group by date(viewed_at)
         182	  ),
         183	  daily_leads as (
         184	    select
         185	      date(created_at) as day,
         186	      count(*) as leads
         187	    from public.leads
         188	    where campaign_id = p_campaign_id
         189	      and (p_start_date is null or created_at >= p_start_date)
         190	      and (p_end_date is null or created_at <= p_end_date)
         191	    group by date(created_at)
         192	  ),
         193	  daily as (
         194	    select
         195	      d.day,
         196	      coalesce(v.visitors, 0) as visitors,
         197	      coalesce(l.leads, 0) as leads
         198	    from (
         199	      select day from daily_views
         200	      union
         201	      select day from daily_leads
         202	    ) d
         203	    left join daily_views v on v.day = d.day
         204	    left join daily_leads l on l.day = d.day
         205	    order by d.day
         206	  )
         207	  select json_build_object(
         208	    'visitors', coalesce((select unique_visitors from view_stats), 0),
         209	    'total_views', coalesce((select total_views from view_stats), 0),
         210	    'leads', coalesce((select total_leads from lead_stats), 0),
         211	    'conversion_rate',
         212	      case
         213	        when coalesce((select unique_visitors from view_stats), 0) = 0 then 0
         214	        else round(
         215	          (coalesce((select total_leads from lead_stats), 0)::numeric /
         216	           nullif((select unique_visitors from view_stats), 0)::numeric) * 100,
         217	          2

         137	@Injectable()
         138	export class AgentLearningLoopPolicyService {
         139	  classifyCandidate(input: AgentLearningCandidateInput): AgentLearningClassification {
         140	    const platformOwned =
         141	      input.ownership === 'platform' ||
         142	      input.artifactKind === 'tool_schema' ||
         143	      input.evidenceKinds.includes('tool_contract_problem')
         144
         145	    if (platformOwned) {
         146	      return this.routeOut(input, 'product_fix_proposal')
         147	    }
         148
         149	    if (input.ownership === 'system') {
         150	      return this.routeOut(input, 'system_artifact_internal_review')
         151	    }
         152
         153	    const agentFileKey = this.resolveAgentFileTarget(input.evidenceKinds)
         154	    if (agentFileKey) {
         155	      return this.customerProposal(input, 'agent_file_update', 'agent_file', agentFileKey)
         156	    }
         157
         158	    if (
         159	      input.artifactKind === 'skill_resource' ||
         160	      input.evidenceKinds.includes('missing_skill_reference')
         161	    ) {
         162	      const skillKey = input.artifactKey ?? input.suggestedSkillKey ?? 'skill-reference'
         163	      return this.customerProposal(input, 'skill_resource_update', 'skill_resource', skillKey)
         164	    }
         165
         166	    if (input.artifactKind === 'skill') {
         167	      const skillKey = input.artifactKey ?? input.suggestedSkillKey ?? 'new-skill'
         168	      const proposalKind = input.artifactKey ? 'skill_update' : 'skill_create'
         169	      return this.customerProposal(input, proposalKind, 'skill', skillKey)
         170	    }
         171

         175	  scoreCandidate(input: AgentLearningScoreInput): AgentLearningScoreResult {
         176	    const scopeFit = this.clamp(input.scopeFit)
         177	    if (scopeFit <= 0) {

         179	        score: 0,
         180	        band: 'blocked',
         181	        eligibleForProposal: false,
         182	        blockedReason: 'scope_fit_failed',
         183	      }
         184	    }
         185
         186	    const weightedScore =
         187	      0.35 * this.clamp(input.userValue) +
         188	      0.25 * this.clamp(input.recurrence) +
         189	      0.2 * this.clamp(input.evidenceConfidence) +
         190	      0.1 * this.clamp(input.blastRadius) +
         191	      0.1 * this.clamp(input.freshness)
         192	    const score = Math.round(weightedScore * scopeFit * 100)
         193	    const band = this.scoreBand(score)
         194
         195	    return {
         196	      score,
         197	      band,
         198	      eligibleForProposal: score >= 55,
         199	      blockedReason: null,
         200	    }

         287	  resolveProposalConflict(input: AgentLearningConflictInput): AgentLearningConflictResult {
         288	    const runningExperiment = input.runningExperiments.find(
         289	      (experiment) =>
         290	        experiment.artifactLockKey === input.artifactLockKey && experiment.status === 'running',
         291	    )
         292	    if (runningExperiment) {
         293	      return {
         294	        action: 'wait_for_running_experiment',
         295	        proposalId: null,
         296	        experimentId: runningExperiment.id,
         297	      }
         298	    }
         299
         300	    const pendingProposal = input.pendingProposals.find(
         301	      (proposal) =>
         302	        proposal.artifactLockKey === input.artifactLockKey && proposal.status === 'pending',
         303	    )
         304	    if (pendingProposal) {
         305	      return {
         306	        action: 'patch_existing_pending_proposal',
         307	        proposalId: pendingProposal.id,
         308	        experimentId: null,
         309	      }
         310	    }
         311
         312	    return {
         313	      action: 'create_new_proposal',
         314	      proposalId: null,
         315	      experimentId: null,
         316	    }
         317	  }

         319	  evaluateProposalQuality(
         320	    input: AgentLearningProposalQualityInput,
         321	  ): AgentLearningProposalQualityResult {
         322	    const failures: string[] = []
         323
         324	    if (input.evidenceEventIds.length < 3) failures.push('minimum_evidence_required')
         325	    if (!input.hasWhy) failures.push('why_required')
         326	    if (!input.hasTrigger) failures.push('trigger_required')
         327	    if (!input.hasDecisionRules) failures.push('decision_rules_required')
         328	    if (!input.hasConcreteExamples) failures.push('concrete_examples_required')
         329	    if (!input.hasExpectedOutput) failures.push('expected_output_required')
         330	    if (input.privateDataRisk !== 'none') failures.push('private_data_risk')
         331
         332	    return {
         333	      ok: failures.length === 0,
         334	      failures,
         335	    }
         336	  }

      ---
      name: 100-sure
      description: A protocol that should be used when editing code to be 100% sure that we follow a specific SOP for context and execution.
      ---

      # 100% Sure Protocol

      ## ⚠️ CONTEXT FIRST (MANDATORY)

      **Before analyzing ANYTHING:**

      1. **Read ENTIRE files (100% of lines)**
         - NEVER read 100 lines of a 600-line file
         - NEVER read "relevant sections" only
         - File is 1000 lines? Read ALL 1000
         - NO EXCEPTIONS

      2. **Read ALL related files**
         - Files that import this file (grep to find)
         - Files this file imports (check imports)
         - Parent components
         - Child components
         - API routes
         - Services used

      3. **Understand complete data flow**
         - Where data comes from
         - How it's transformed (every step)
         - Where it goes
         - Who uses it

      **Context Checklist - ALL must be checked:**

      - [ ] Read ENTIRE target file (100% of lines)
      - [ ] Read ALL importing files
      - [ ] Read ALL imported files
      - [ ] Understand complete data flow
      - [ ] Found all usages (grep)
      - [ ] Checked git history
      - [ ] Know how change fits in system

      **If ANY box unchecked → STOP. DO NOT EDIT.**

      ---

      ## ⚠️ DEAD CODE REMOVAL (MANDATORY)

      **After creating NEW code, remove OLD code it replaces.**

      ### Quick Protocol

      1. **Created new code?** → What does it replace?
      2. **Find old code** → Use grep to find all usages
      3. **Confidence check:**
         - **≥90%** safe to remove → Remove it
         - **<90%** → ASK USER before removing

      ### Removal Checklist

      - [ ] New code replaces something old?
      - [ ] Grepped for old code usages?
      - [ ] ≥90% confident OR asked user?
      - [ ] Removed old files in same change?
      - [ ] Removed from barrel exports (index.ts)?

      **Template for asking user (when <90% confident):**

      ```
      I created [new code].

      OLD CODE: [file/path]
      USAGES: [locations found]
      CONFIDENCE: [X]%
      CONCERN: [why uncertain]

      Should I remove the old code?
      ```

      **If ANY unchecked → STOP. Complete cleanup.**

      ---

      ## Pre-Edit Verification

      Before editing ANY line of code, verify:

      1. **Read the actual file** (ENTIRELY, not from memory)
      2. **Quote the exact line** you're changing
      3. **Verify no dependencies** break
      4. **State why this specific LOC** needs changing
      5. **Verified complete context** (checklist above)

      ## Execution Rules

      - Context gathering is MANDATORY (see above)
      - Pay extra attention while editing
      - Do not modify anything beyond what's required
      - Make edits in very small, focused steps
      - ONLY change a LOC once you are 100% certain it's the correct one
      - NEVER make quick fixes without full context

      ## Evidence Format

      Before each edit:
      File: [exact path]
      Current line [X]: [exact current code]
      Changing to: [exact new code]
      Reason: [specific reason]
      Dependencies checked: [list]
      Confidence: 100%

      ## Failure Mode

      If you can't provide evidence above → STOP and ask questions.

      name: meticulously

      ---

      # System Prompt — "Meticulous Code Analyst (Zero-Assumption Mode)"

      **Role:**
      You are a Meticulous Code Analyst. Your identity is precision. You analyze code, diagnose bugs, and plan features with absolute thoroughness. You never speculate. You verify every claim against evidence. You read everything provided, enumerate unknowns, and test hypotheses systematically. You do not ship an answer until you have checked every plausible angle.

      ## ⚠️ CRITICAL: CONTEXT GATHERING PROTOCOL (MANDATORY)

      **BEFORE analyzing ANY code, you MUST:**

      1. **Read ENTIRE files (100% of lines)**
         - Never read excerpts or "relevant sections"
         - File is 600 lines? Read all 600
         - File is 1500 lines? Read all 1500
         - "Too long" is NOT an excuse

      2. **Read ALL related files**
         - Every file that imports the target file (use grep)
         - Every file the target imports
         - Parent components/containers
         - Child components
         - API routes it calls
         - Services it uses

      3. **Understand COMPLETE data flow**
         - Data origin (database, API, props, state)
         - All transformations (every function touching it)
         - Data destination (render, storage, child components)
         - All consumers (who uses this?)

      **Context Verification Checklist:**

      Before starting analysis, verify:

      - [ ] I read the ENTIRE target file (100% of lines)
      - [ ] I read ALL files that import this file
      - [ ] I read ALL files this file imports
      - [ ] I understand complete data flow
      - [ ] I searched for all usages (grep)
      - [ ] I checked git history for WHY this exists
      - [ ] I can explain how it fits in the system

      **If ANY box unchecked → STOP. Gather context first. DO NOT PROCEED.**

      **Your (Codex's) Known Weaknesses:**

      - ❌ Reading partial files and assuming understanding
      - ❌ Making quick fixes without full context
      - ❌ Skipping "unrelated" files
      - ❌ Focusing on symptoms not root causes

      **You MUST combat these by forcing yourself to read EVERYTHING related.**

      ---

      ## ⚠️ CRITICAL: DEAD CODE REMOVAL PROTOCOL (MANDATORY)

      **When creating NEW code that replaces OLD code, you MUST remove the old code.**

      ### The Removal Problem

      You (Codex) tend to:

      - ❌ Create new hook → Leave old hook file
      - ❌ Extract service → Don't delete inline code
      - ❌ Create new type → Leave old type
      - ❌ Refactor component → Old component remains

      **Result:** Multiple versions, technical debt, confusion about which to use.

      ### Mandatory Protocol

      **After creating new code:**

      1. **Identify what it replaces**
         - New version of existing code?
         - Extracted from inline logic?
         - Replaces old pattern?

      2. **Find ALL old code** (use grep)

         ```bash
         grep -r "OldName" src/
         ```

      3. **Confidence check**
         - **≥90% confident** safe to remove → Remove it
         - **<90% confident** → ASK USER:
           ```
           I created [new]. Found OLD: [file].
           CONFIDENCE: [X]%. CONCERN: [reason]
           Should I remove old code?
           ```

      4. **Remove in SAME change**
         - Delete old files
         - Update all references
         - Remove exports from index.ts
         - Document in changelog

      ### Checklist Before Completion

      - [ ] Created something NEW that replaces OLD?
      - [ ] Grepped for all usages of old code?
      - [ ] ≥90% confident OR asked user?
      - [ ] Removed old code/files?
      - [ ] Updated all imports?
      - [ ] Removed from barrel exports?

      **If ANY unchecked → STOP. Clean up or ask user.**

      ---

      **Non-Negotiables:**

      - **No speculation.** If data is missing, explicitly list the gaps and what evidence is required.
      - **Evidence over opinion.** Cite exact files, functions, lines, logs, stack traces, and repro steps.
      - **Single-source truth.** Prefer repository state and runtime behavior over memory or guesses.
      - **Smallest details matter.** Names, nullability, types, ranges, encodings, timezones, locales, concurrency, memory, I/O, network, permissions, config, build flags, environment, versions.
      - **Security & correctness first.** Any change must preserve safety, idempotence where needed, and backward compatibility (unless explicitly allowed).
      - **COMPLETE context first.** Never analyze code without reading entire files and all dependencies.

      **Required Inputs (ask/derive as needed, never assume):**

      1. Code scope (repo/paths)
      2. Runtime context (OS, architecture, container, env vars, secrets strategy)
      3. Versions (language, framework, libs, build tools)
      4. Exact error (full logs/trace, timestamps)
      5. Reproduction steps (commands, seeds, fixtures, data shape)
      6. Expected vs. actual behavior
      7. Constraints (perf budgets, latency/throughput, memory, SLAs, security/compliance)
      8. Acceptance criteria & definition of done

      **Operating Modes:**

      ### 1) Bug/Incident Analysis (“Bug Hunter”)

      Process:

      - **Understand:** Restate the symptom, scope impact, blast radius, first-seen time, recent changes (commits, deps, infra).
      - **Reproduce:** Create minimal, deterministic repro. Note all conditions (seed, locale, tz, CPU count, feature flags).
      - **Triage:** Classify (logic error, race, resource leak, state drift, boundary, config, IO, permissions, API contract, data quality, encoding).
      - **Root Cause:** Use evidence (stack frames, invariants, failing assertions, state diffs). Disprove alternatives.
      - **Fix Options:** Present ≥2 viable paths with trade-offs (risk, complexity, perf, blast radius).
      - **Verify:** Add/adjust tests; run static/type checks, lints, build; re-run repro; confirm no regressions.
      - **Prevent:** Propose guardrails (asserts, types, retries/backoff, circuit breakers, input validation, monitors, SLO alerts).

      ### 2) Feature Planning (“Feature Architect”)

      Process:

      - **Requirements digestion:** Translate request into precise, testable acceptance criteria & non-functionals.
      - **Design:** Outline API contracts, data models, state transitions, error taxonomy, concurrency model, idempotency, migrations, rollout plan (flags), and de-risk spikes.
      - **Impact Mapping:** Identify affected modules, boundaries, external services, schemas, and compatibility concerns.
      - **Plan:** Deliver a phased plan with tasks, estimates, risks, fallbacks, and observability (metrics, logs, traces).
      - **Spec → Tests → Code:** Propose test matrix first (unit/integration/e2e/property/fuzz), then implementation sketch.

      **Universal Deep-Dive Checklist (apply in every task):**

      - Types & Nullability (optional vs. required, undefined vs. null)
      - Bounds & Ranges (off-by-one, index, length, pagination)
      - State & Concurrency (races, locks, deadlocks, async flows, promises/futures)
      - Time & Locale (UTC vs. local, DST, leap seconds, ISO8601, parsing/format)
      - I/O & Networking (timeouts, retries, backoff, idempotency, partial failures)
      - Data Contracts (schema versioning, migrations, serialization, encodings, emoji/unicode)
      - Config & Env (feature flags, prod vs. dev parity, secrets loading)
      - Build/Tooling (compiler flags, tree-shaking, minification, source maps)
      - Performance (allocations, N+1 queries, Big-O hotspots, streaming vs. buffering)
      - Security (injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, path traversal, authZ/authN, secrets handling, PII logging)
      - Testing (happy paths, edge cases, fuzz, property-based, flaky tests, hermeticity)
      - Observability (structured logs, metrics, traces, correlation IDs)
      - Dependencies (version drift, transitive risks, known CVEs, breaking changes)

      **Output Format (always use — TWO LAYERS):**

      Present findings in TWO layers. Always lead with the Architect Summary. Follow with Technical Evidence only after the summary is complete.

      ### Layer 1: Architect Summary (ALWAYS FIRST)

      Write this for someone who builds the product but doesn't read code. No file names, no function names, no jargon. Use real-world analogies (phone calls, receptionists, assembly lines, post offices, etc.) to make system behavior intuitive.

      Structure:

      1. **What's happening right now** — Describe the current behavior in plain language. What does the user experience? What's going wrong? Use a concrete scenario ("User sends a message, switches tabs, comes back, sees nothing running...").

      2. **Why it's happening** — Explain the root cause as a concept, not as code. ("We built two copies of the truth — one in memory, one in the database — and they disagree." NOT "The StreamRegistry state drifts from the messages table.")

      3. **What the options are** — Present each fix/approach as a clear trade-off the reader can evaluate without technical knowledge. ("Option A gives you instant status but needs the server to be running. Option B survives server restarts but has a small delay.") Always include your recommendation and why.

      4. **What changes** — In simple terms, what gets simpler, what gets removed, what the user will experience differently. ("When you disconnect and come back, instead of seeing nothing, you'll immediately see 'Agent is working' and the content will update every 2 seconds until it's done.")

      Rules for Layer 1:

      - NO file paths, function names, class names, or variable names
      - NO code snippets or line numbers
      - Use analogies to explain system concepts (connections = phone calls, caches = receptionists, databases = filing cabinets, etc.)
      - Short paragraphs. One idea per paragraph.
      - Write as if explaining to the CEO, not to a developer
      - When presenting options, frame them as decisions with trade-offs, not implementation details

      ### Layer 2: Technical Evidence (AFTER the summary)

      This is the proof. Every claim in Layer 1 must be backed by evidence here. This layer is for verification and implementation, not for understanding.

      Structure:

      1. **Evidence Pack** — Exact files, line numbers, code snippets, logs, stack traces, queries that prove each claim in Layer 1
      2. **Root Cause Chain** — The "5 Whys" trace with code-level proof at each step
      3. **Patch Sketch** — Diff or pseudocode for the recommended fix
      4. **Impact Map** — Which files change, what depends on them, what could break
      5. **Test Plan** — Cases, data, edge cases, regression checks
      6. **Risk & Rollout** — Feature flags, canaries, monitoring, rollback plan
      7. **Quality Control Summary**
         - Instructions fully covered?
         - All checklists passed?
         - Unknowns explicitly listed?
         - Repro verified post-fix?
         - New tests added and running clean?

      **Quality Bar (“Refusal to Assume”):**
      If any required input is missing, do **not** guess. Produce:

      - A **Missing Evidence List** (bullet points)
      - The **smallest experiment** to obtain each piece (command/log/query)
      - The **impact of proceeding without it** (risk statement)

      **Tone & Style:**

      - **Layer 1:** Conversational, clear, analogy-driven. Like explaining to a smart founder who doesn't code. Every sentence should pass the test: "Would a non-developer understand this?"
      - **Layer 2:** Precise, concise, technical. File paths, line references, code snippets. Every claim checkable against the codebase.

      .docs/logs/changelog2026-08-19.md:328:What: Submitting a new chat from Home no longer flashes the half-loaded agent identity. A queued send seed (or its in-flight application) now suppresses the empty-chat agent hero and shows a small sending skeleton until the optimistic message lands (isPendingSendSeedForPanel + seedSendInFlight gate in SpaceVibeyChatPanel).
      .docs/logs/changelog2026-08-19.md:331:Files: apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/chat/SpaceVibeyChatPanel.tsx, apps/web/src/components/global-chat/lib/global-chat-seed-match.ts(+test)
      .docs/logs/changelog2026-08-19.md:335:What: Recents filter fixes. (1) Clicking a chat under an active filter no longer gets hijacked or stranded: /home?conv= now beats a lingering meeting context in GlobalChatPanel (the meeting thread could shadow the clicked conversation — "opens then goes away"), and a conversation whose messages are still hydrating shows a "Loading conversation…" skeleton instead of a blank pane (SpaceVibeyChatPanel; empty-chat hero suppressed only while hydration is pending). (2) The scope picker's program-less campaigns render under their own "Campaigns" section label instead of inside "Programs" — "Claude Club Webinar" / "Master Your Kraft | VSL …" are campaigns, not programs; the Programs label only renders when a real program has campaigns.
      .docs/logs/changelog2026-08-19.md:338:Files: apps/web/src/components/global-chat/containers/GlobalChatPanel.tsx, apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/chat/SpaceVibeyChatPanel.tsx, apps/web/src/components/conversations/ConversationScopePickerMenus.tsx, conversation-scope-picker.messages.config.ts
      .docs/logs/changelog2026-08-19.md:360:What: Pixel identity + mission↔chat wiring fixes. (1) `normalizeDefaultAgentIdentity` now keeps a custom `agents_registry.image_url` (onboarding portrait) and only falls back to the lamp `/pixel-avatar.png` when the row has no avatar — chat roster now matches mission Activity/Assignees. (2) Mission detail modal emits a `mission:detail-focus` window event; SpaceVibeyChatPanel tracks it and `resolveChatSendAwarenessContext` appends an "Open mission: … (mission, id, status)" line on every chat surface, so main-chat messages sent while a mission panel is open carry the mission id. (3) `add_mission_comment` (agent-api) stamps the acting agent key (from the session key, not model input); the missions API stores it on the `user.comment` log (`agent_key` column + `commented_by_agent_key` payload, both lifecycle paths) and the Activity timeline renders agent-relayed comments with the agent header instead of the viewer's own name/avatar.

           1	# Task-Agent Artifact Output Gap Audit
           2
           3	Generated: 2026-06-24
           4
           5	## Purpose
           6
           7	Audit whether artifacts or Space items created by agents while running inside a task reliably appear in both places users expect:
           8
           9	- inline task activity as the same preview card style used in chat
          10	- the task detail Deliverables & media carousel
          11
          12	This audit covers the task-agent path, the OpenClaw tool stream bridge, backend artifact action results, frontend content-block-to-deliverable mapping, and the reported production task `d6a1b64a-ab00-4bab-87a3-06cb521b3fbb`.
          13
          14	## Result Summary
          15
          16	- The production test only created documents plus one follow-up task item. No funnels, presentations, ads, media, forms, or posts were created in that run.
          17	- 2026-06-25 update: task completion now reconciles scoped persisted outputs after the stream merge. The readback covers Space Docs, created Space items/tasks, offers, avatars, sequences, renderable presentations, renderable funnels/websites, social posts, ads/ad sets/ad campaigns, forms, flows, task-linked emails, and media assets.
          18	- Remaining fallback gaps are output families that either do not persist a safely task-scoped row, do not have a stable previewable row shape, or still need producer-side block work.
          19	- The frontend can convert `artifact_preview`, `document_card`, `media_asset`, `pdf_file`, `docx_file`, `project_preview`, `widget_preview`, and `browser_screenshot` blocks into task deliverables, but not every backend output emits or persists enough scope to reconstruct one.
          20
          21	Critical conclusion: the old document-only fallback has been replaced with a scoped generic readback for the main persisted artifact families; unsupported or unscoped producer actions still need targeted cleanup before the platform can claim every possible durable output has a DB fallback.
          22
          23	## Current Data Flow
          24
          25	1. Backend artifact action executes through `ArtifactActionExecutionService`.
          26	2. If the action result includes `ui_blocks`, `OpenClawStreamToolService` emits each as `ui_block`.
          27	3. `TaskAgentProgressService` appends `ui_block` events to task activity `payload.content_blocks_ordered`.
          28	4. `TaskAgentService` completes the activity with the final blocks.
          29	5. `TaskAgentArtifactOutputsService` adds missing scoped persisted output blocks for supported artifact tables, task-linked emails, media assets, Space Docs, and created Space items.
          30	6. `collectTaskDeliverablesFromActivity` converts final blocks into `MissionDeliverable` rows for the task carousel using `missionDeliverableFromContentBlock`.
          31
          32	## Covered Today
          33
          34	| Output family | Producer block | Deliverable mapping | Task fallback | Current status |
          35	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
          36	| Space Docs via `save_document` | `document_card` | `doc` | Yes | Covered |
          37	| PDF via `create_pdf` | `document_card` from service | `doc` | Yes, if mirrored as Space Doc | Mostly covered |
          38	| DOCX via `create_docx` | `document_card` from service | `doc` | Yes, if mirrored as Space Doc | Mostly covered |
          39	| Offer via `create_offer` | `artifact_preview: offer` | `offer` | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
          40	| Ad via `create_ad` | `artifact_preview: ad` | `ad` or `image` if image URL exists | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
          41	| Ad campaign via `create_ad_campaign` | `artifact_preview: ad-campaign` | `ad_campaign` | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
          42	| Funnel via `create_funnel` | `artifact_preview: funnel` | `funnel` | Yes, when renderable by home page/pages/files | Covered for renderable rows |
          43	| Funnel page via `add_funnel_page` | `artifact_preview: funnel` with `funnelPageId` | `funnel` | Yes, via parent funnel renderability | Covered |
          44	| Presentation via `create_presentation` | `artifact_preview: presentation` | `presentation` | Yes, when generated HTML or files exist | Covered for renderable rows |
          45	| Sequence via `create_sequence` | `artifact_preview: sequence` | `sequence` | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
          46	| Avatar via `create_avatar` | `artifact_preview: avatar` | `avatar` or `image` if image URL exists | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
          47	| Email via `save_email` | `artifact_preview: email` | `email` | Yes, when linked to the task `source_item_id` | Covered |
          48	| Social post via `create_social_post` | `artifact_preview: social-post` | `social_post` or media if image/video URL exists | Yes, scoped row readback | Covered |
          49	| Blog post via `create_blog_post` | `artifact_preview: blog-post` | `blog_post` or `image` if cover exists | No | Stream-dependent |
          50
          51	## Gaps
          52
          53	| Output family | Gap | Impact | Priority |
          54	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
          55	| Out-of-catalog or unscoped artifact previews | No safe task completion reconciliation when the durable row lacks task Space scope or the output has no stable previewable persisted row. | A successfully created artifact can still be absent if the stream block is missed and DB readback cannot safely identify it. | P0 |
          56	| Generated images and videos | `generate_image` / `generate_video` fallback emits a text markdown link, not a structured media block. | It may look visible in chat text but the task carousel ignores it. | P0 |
          57	| Processed media | `process_media` returns `url` and `media_asset_id` but no `ui_blocks`; extractor does not synthesize one. | Processed images/videos/audio are not task deliverables unless another path attaches them. | P0 |
          58	| Forms | `create_form`, `publish_form`, and `attach_form_asset` return form data/URL only; task readback now covers scoped created form rows. | Producer-side blocks are still missing, but task completion can recover created forms. | P1 |
          59	| Tasks / generic Space items | `create_task` creates `space_items` but returns raw task data only; task readback now covers non-doc Space items created in the same scoped run. | Producer-side blocks are still missing, but task completion can recover created task/custom item rows. | P1 |
          60	| Missions | `create_mission` creates/ensures Mission view and indexes the source but returns raw mission data only. No block or mapper support. | Chat-created missions can exist without a task output card. | P1 |
          61	| Contacts | `create_contact` returns raw contact data only; no block or mapper support. | Created contacts do not appear as task deliverables. | P1 |
          62	| Flows | `create_flow_draft` and `publish_flow` return raw `space_automations`; task readback now covers scoped rows created by the task actor. | Producer-side blocks are still missing, but task completion can recover created flow rows. | P1 |
          63	| Projects/code artifacts | Frontend supports `project_preview`, but `create_project` returns the main API result and does not synthesize `project_preview`. | Code/project outputs are not guaranteed in task deliverables. | P1 |
          64	| Websites | `create_website` is implemented through the funnel path and emits `artifact_preview: funnel`; frontend has a `website` deliverable type but the block contract does not expose `website`. | Website outputs are typed as funnels in task deliverables. | P2 |
          65	| Visual docs | `generate_visual_html` emits `artifact_preview: visual-doc`; frontend block union accepts it, but deliverable mapper does not map it. | Visual docs can render in chat but not become typed task deliverables. | P2 |
          66	| Email sequence emails | `add_sequence_email` emits an `artifact_preview` with `artifactType: sequence` and the parent sequence id, not the sequence email id/type. | Individual email outputs inside a sequence are attributed to the sequence, not the email draft. | P2 |
          67	| Ad sets and bulk ads | `create_ad_set` and `bulk_create_ads` return raw data without `artifact_preview` blocks. | Created ad-set/bulk ad output is not guaranteed in task deliverables. | P2 |
          68	| Branding themes | `create_theme` returns raw theme data only; no deliverable type or block mapping. | Agent-created themes are not task output cards. | P2 |
          69	| Custom objects | `define_object_type` and `create_object` return raw rows only. | Custom Space/customer objects are invisible in task output cards. | P2 |
          70
          71	## Recommended Fix Order
          72
          73	1. Replace the document-only fallback with a generic `TaskAgentArtifactBlocksService`.
          74	   - Keep the existing Space Doc logic.
          75	   - Add table-backed reconciliation for `artifact_preview`, media, tasks/Space items, missions, forms, flows, contacts, projects, themes, and custom objects.
          76	   - Deduplicate against existing streamed blocks by entity table/id.
          77
          78	2. Extend the shared block and deliverable contracts.
          79	   - Add or map `form`, `website`, `visual-doc`, `media_asset`, `task`, `mission`, `contact`, `flow`, `theme`, and `custom_object`.
          80	   - Add a structured media block instead of using markdown `text` for generated images/videos.
          81
          82	3. Fix producer actions that create durable outputs without blocks.
          83	   - `create_form`, `publish_form`, `create_task`, `create_mission`, `create_contact`, `create_flow_draft`, `publish_flow`, `create_project`, `create_theme`, `create_object`, `process_media`, `create_ad_set`, `bulk_create_ads`.
          84
          85	4. Add guardrail tests.
          86	   - Backend: every durable create/save/generate action either returns a deliverable-capable block or is explicitly classified as not a deliverable.
          87	   - Task agent: reconciliation adds missing blocks for each supported table.
          88	   - Frontend: every supported block maps to a task deliverable and category.
          89	   - Stream bridge: `ui_blocks` from direct, nested, and text-envelope tool results are persisted into task activity.
          90
          91	## Acceptance Criteria
          92
          93	- A task-agent run that creates each supported output type ends with a matching block in `space_item_activity.payload.content_blocks_ordered`.
          94	- The task detail Deliverables & media carousel shows each output without depending on a perfect live stream.
          95	- Chat and task activity use the same block contracts for preview cards.
          96	- Each durable create/save/generate action is classified as one of:
          97	  - previewable deliverable
          98	  - non-deliverable side effect
          99	  - confirmation/clarification/status-only UI
         100	- Production verification can query recent task-run entities and match them to task activity blocks by entity table/id.

      documentation/features/spaces-automation.md:21:- One scheduled `observe_slack_team` action powers Pixel Team intelligence. Slack webhook messages enter `slack_observation_events` once; a five-minute analysis schedule consumes only events after an exact cursor, while an hourly reconciliation pass catches missed channel messages and expands threads. Empty five-minute intervals make no model call and do not re-analyze prior messages. Public channels are discovered and joined automatically when the installed Slack token includes `channels:join`; newly joined channels are reconciled immediately so historical context enters the ledger. Administrators can exclude channels from observation, and Team → People → Channels reports discovered, joined, observed, excluded, and inaccessible coverage. Private channels remain invite-only in Slack. A new consumer recovers from the oldest stored ledger event, so a provider outage cannot strand evidence outside a moving lookback window. The analyzer examines every non-Ignored human sender in the selected channels, detects Person Brain facts, repeated workflows, unanswered questions, and client-risk signals together, then advances only after the run succeeds. `person_ids` is not a source-sender filter: it restricts Active recipients, Person Brain compounding, and personal-moment outreach. Large windows are processed in bounded 250-message batches rather than silently dropping later channels. The analyzer uses direct Gemini with a strict response schema and low reasoning level, rejects signals without exact source evidence or at least 80% confidence, resolves the finding's subject from that event's sender, registers previously unseen human senders as durable Manage People records, snapshots readable channel/person/time/source-text evidence onto every proposal, and records exact token usage plus provider cost. Unmatched Slack identities default to External unless they match a portal teammate or retain a manual classification. An explicitly enabled managed Person Brain compounds verified facts in Shadow mode because Brain learning is an internal permission, separate from outbound delivery. Findings about external or ignored people remain internal-only Signals and never enter that external person's DM path; when the connected workspace owner maps to an Internal Slack person, Pixel also creates a separate internal follow-up linked to the signal. Operational alerts enter a cooling lifecycle before delivery: client-risk findings wait 15 minutes, unanswered questions wait 30 minutes, workflow/context briefing signals wait 60 minutes, and personal moments wait about 8 minutes before a standalone Active DM. Personal moments stay off the numbered EOD digest path. At eligibility Pixel refreshes the exact source thread and reactions. Resolved findings are dismissed without messaging, unavailable source evidence remains reviewable, and only still-unresolved alerts addressed to an Internal person who is individually Active can be delivered outside quiet hours. Post-call recaps use their separate confirmation flow and remain immediate. Shadow and Off recipients keep reviewable proposals. In Signals, an administrator can add an instruction, optionally save it as a reusable playbook rule, and create one or more internal Shadow drafts. Multiple named internal recipients create a group-DM draft; external and ignored recipients are filtered again before proposal creation and delivery. Disabled is Off; Shadow continues detection and creates reviewable proposals for recipients who are not individually Active. Other Active actions can send an internal message only when both explicit channel/person allowlists exist and the recipient is classified Internal and individually Active.       documentation/features/spaces-automation.md:26:- Vercel calls the CRON_SECRET-protected `/api/internal/space-automations/process-due` endpoint every minute. The endpoint invokes the due-schedule scanner; its database compare-and-swap claim prevents duplicate execution. In-process schedule polling is off by default and requires `SPACE_AUTOMATION_IN_PROCESS_CRON_ENABLED=1` on a persistent host, so unrelated Vercel cron requests cannot race the dedicated endpoint. Each scan also repairs enabled published schedule rows whose materialized next-fire is null. Invalid cron expressions remain disabled; transient persistence failures leave the due timestamp untouched for retry. Scheduled agent actions do not pre-wake Fly in the scheduler. `SpaceAutomationService` calls `UserAgentApiService` for agent execution, so shared Railway profiles route to the shared Agent API/OpenClaw runtime and Fly-machine profiles wake through the shared runtime service path when needed.

          11	/**
          12	 * OrgContextGuard — extracts X-Org-Id from request headers, verifies active membership,
          13	 * and attaches orgId + orgRole to the request.
          14	 *
          15	 * When no X-Org-Id header: personal context (orgId = null, orgRole = null).
          16	 * When X-Org-Id present: verifies user is active member, attaches role.
          17	 *
          18	 * Must run AFTER AuthGuard (needs request.user.id).
          19	 */
          20	@Injectable()
          21	export class OrgContextGuard implements CanActivate {
          22	  private readonly logger = new Logger(OrgContextGuard.name)
          23
          24	  constructor(private readonly serviceClient: SupabaseServiceClient) {}
          25
          26	  async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
          27	    const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest()
          28	    const orgId = request.headers['x-org-id'] as string | undefined
          29	    const userId = request.user?.id
          30
          31	    if (!orgId) {
          32	      request.orgId = null
          33	      request.orgRole = null
          34	      request.orgMemberId = null
          35	      request.organizationWideDataAccess = false
          36	      return true
          37	    }
          38
          39	    if (!userId) {
          40	      throw new ForbiddenException('Authentication required for org context')
          41	    }
          42
          43	    const { data: membership, error } = await this.serviceClient.client
          44	      .from('org_members')
          45	      .select('id, role, status, ai_data_admin')
          46	      .eq('org_id', orgId)
          47	      .eq('user_id', userId)
          48	      .maybeSingle()
          49
          50	    if (error) {
          51	      this.logger.error(`Org membership lookup failed: ${error.message}`)
          52	      throw new ForbiddenException('Organization access verification failed')
          53	    }
          54
          55	    if (!membership || membership.status !== 'active') {
          56	      throw new ForbiddenException('You are not an active member of this organization')
          57	    }
          58
          59	    request.orgId = orgId
          60	    request.orgRole = membership.role as OrgRole
          61	    request.orgMemberId = membership.id
          62	    request.organizationWideDataAccess =
          63	      membership.role === 'owner' || membership.ai_data_admin === true
          64
          65	    return true
          66	  }
          67	}
          25
          26	const ORG_ROLE_HIERARCHY: Record<OrgRole, number> = {
          27	  owner: 5,
          28	  admin: 4,
          29	  creator: 3,
          30	  editor: 2,
          31	  viewer: 1,
          32	}
          33
          34	/**
          35	 * OrgRoleGuard — checks if user's org role meets the minimum required by @RequireOrgRole().
          36	 *
          37	 * Must run AFTER AuthGuard + OrgContextGuard (needs request.orgId + request.orgRole).
          38	 *
          39	 * Behavior:
          40	 * - No @RequireOrgRole() decorator: passes through (no role check)
          41	 * - Not in org context (orgId = null): passes through (personal context, no org role needed)
          42	 * - In org context: checks orgRole >= requiredRole
          43	 */
          44	@Injectable()
          45	export class OrgRoleGuard implements CanActivate {
          46	  private readonly logger = new Logger(OrgRoleGuard.name)
          47	  private readonly reflector = new Reflector()
          48
          49	  async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
          50	    const requiredRole = this.reflector.getAllAndOverride<OrgRole | undefined>(ORG_ROLE_KEY, [
          51	      context.getHandler(),
          52	      context.getClass(),
          53	    ])
          54
          55	    if (!requiredRole) {
          56	      return true
          57	    }
          58
          59	    const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest()
          60	    const orgId = request.orgId
          61	    const orgRole = request.orgRole as OrgRole | null
          62
          63	    if (!orgId) {
          64	      return true
          65	    }
          66
          67	    if (!orgRole) {
          68	      throw new ForbiddenException('Organization role not resolved')
          69	    }
          70
          71	    const userLevel = ORG_ROLE_HIERARCHY[orgRole]
          72	    const requiredLevel = ORG_ROLE_HIERARCHY[requiredRole]
          73
          74	    if (userLevel < requiredLevel) {
          75	      throw new ForbiddenException(
          76	        `This action requires "${requiredRole}" role. Your role is "${orgRole}".`,
          77	      )
          78	    }
          79
          80	    return true
          81	  }
          82	}
